note: Generic 16-week foundation plan for a working professional (~2 h on weeknights, ~7 h on Saturday, Sunday test + revision, ~24 h/week). Week 1 starts on any Monday; weekday labels are relative. Run scripts/make_plan.py with the learner's real start and Prelims dates to put calendar dates on it. Built as an example for a start of Mon 2 Nov 2026 with Prelims assumed 23 May 2027.
profile: working professional, Mon-Fri 10pm-12am, Sat 7-8h, Sun test+revision

blocks.name: Polity

weeks.theme: Constitutional Framework: from Historical Background to Basic Structure, plus Fundamental Rights

days.task: Laxmikanth, 'Historical Background': go from the Regulating Act 1773 to the Indian Independence Act 1947 and make a table with one line per Act saying what it introduced first. Then 'Making of the Constitution': composition of the Constituent Assembly, its major committees and their chairmen, the Objectives Resolution and the enactment and enforcement dates. Skim the criticism section.
days.pyq: Polity PYQs 2013-2026 on the Charter Acts, the Indian Councils Act 1909, the Government of India Acts 1919 and 1935, the Cabinet Mission and the Constituent Assembly. Note the ones that overlap with Modern History.
days.tip: UPSC asks which Act first introduced something, e.g. separate electorates (Indian Councils Act 1909), dyarchy (GoI Act 1919) or provincial autonomy and federal court (GoI Act 1935). Memorise these firsts. You do not need every clause of every Act.

days.task: 'Salient Features of the Constitution': borrowed features by country, the blend of parliamentary and federal features, and federal structure with a unitary bias. Make a one-line-each list of the 12 Schedules (what each contains). Then 'Preamble': the text word by word, its ingredients, the Berubari, Kesavananda and LIC (1995) cases, and the 42nd Amendment additions.
days.pyq: PYQs on the Preamble, the sources of borrowed features, the Schedules and questions on the 'ideals/philosophy of the Constitution', 2013-2026.
days.tip: Learn the Preamble text word for word, because UPSC tests the exact order of the words. Keep a one-page 'feature → source country' table, e.g. Directive Principles from Ireland, residuary powers from Canada, concurrent list from Australia. Keep the 12-Schedules list on the same page; 'Schedule → subject' pairs are a favourite match-type question.

days.task: 'Union and its Territory': Articles 1-4, Parliament's power to reorganise states by simple majority, and the 100th Amendment (Land Boundary Agreement with Bangladesh). Skim the year-by-year chronology of state formation. Then 'Citizenship': Articles 5-11, how citizenship is acquired and lost under the Citizenship Act 1955 (including the 2019 amendment, CAA), single citizenship, and OCI. Skim the PIO history.
days.pyq: PYQs on the Article 3 procedure, acquiring and losing citizenship, and OCI, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Common trap: an Article 3 bill needs the President's prior recommendation and he must refer it to the state legislature for its views. Those views are not binding on Parliament. Laws made under Article 4 are not treated as Article 368 amendments.

days.task: 'Directive Principles of State Policy': Articles 36-51, classified as socialistic, Gandhian or liberal-intellectual. Note the new DPSPs added by the 42nd, 44th, 86th and 97th Amendments, and the FR-versus-DPSP conflict cases (Champakam, Golaknath, Kesavananda, Minerva Mills). Then 'Fundamental Duties': the 11 duties in Article 51A, the Swaran Singh Committee and the Verma Committee. Skim the criticism.
days.pyq: PYQs on how DPSPs are classified, DPSP versus FR, and the list of Fundamental Duties, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Start a 3-column sheet: Fundamental Right / Directive Principle / Fundamental Duty. Fill the DPSP and FD columns tonight and complete the FR column after Saturday's FR chapter. Example: education for ages 6-14 appears as Article 21A (FR), Article 45 (DPSP) and Article 51A(k) (FD); the environment appears as Article 48A (DPSP) and Article 51A(g) (FD). UPSC likes questions that mix these up.

days.task: 'Amendment of the Constitution': the Article 368 procedure, the three kinds of amendment (simple majority, special majority, special majority plus ratification by half the states), and the fact that Presidential assent became compulsory after the 24th Amendment. Then 'Basic Structure of the Constitution': the line Shankari Prasad → Golaknath → Kesavananda → Indira Gandhi (1975) → Minerva Mills, and the list of basic-structure elements.
days.pyq: PYQs on Article 368, special majority, state ratification and the basic structure doctrine, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Make a 'which majority?' table. Simple majority outside Article 368: Articles 2, 3 and 169, the 5th and 6th Schedules. Special majority: Fundamental Rights and DPSPs. Special majority plus half the states: election of the President, Seventh Schedule, representation of states in Parliament, GST.

days.task:
(7 Nov, tough chapters in the 3h slot) 'Fundamental Rights' in full, Articles 12-35. Cover:
- the definition of State (Art 12) and Art 13
- equality, Arts 14-18, with the reservation cases (Indra Sawhney, the 103rd Amendment on EWS)
- the six freedoms of Art 19 and their reasonable restrictions
- Arts 20-22, including preventive detention
- Arts 23-24
- freedom of religion, Arts 25-28
- cultural and educational rights, Arts 29-30
- Art 32 and the five writs
- Arts 33-35
Then 'Parliamentary System': its features, and how the Indian system differs from the British one.
days.pyq: 2h block: all FR PYQs from 2013-2026 (the biggest pool in Polity). Then make a one-page table with the columns Article | Right | Citizens only or all persons | Landmark case, and complete the FR column of Thursday's FR/DPSP/FD sheet.
days.tip: Two traps come up again and again. First, which FRs are for citizens only (15, 16, 19, 29, 30) and which are for all persons. Second, which writ lies against whom: mandamus does not lie against the President, a Governor or a private person, but habeas corpus lies even against a private person.

days.task: 9:30-11:30 weekly test of 50 MCQs on the Week 1 portion: Historical Background through Basic Structure, Fundamental Rights and Parliamentary System. Then the mistake log: label each wrong answer as a concept gap, a fact gap or a misread trap. Revise the FR table, the DPSP/FD sheet, the Schedules list and the Preamble. Clear any weekday backlog.
days.pyq: Re-attempt every PYQ you got wrong this week (FRs, DPSP, Article 368) without looking at the answers.
days.tip: For every mistake, add one 'never again' line to your short notes, e.g. 'Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency'. This list becomes your revision sheet for the final month.

weeks.theme: System of Government and the Union: Federalism, Emergency, President, PM and Council of Ministers, Parliament

days.task: 'Federal System': federal and unitary features, the 'quasi-federal' label and the Supreme Court's view in Bommai. Then 'Inter-State Relations': water disputes (Art 262), the Inter-State Council (Art 263), full faith and credit, inter-state trade (Arts 301-307) and Zonal Councils. Skim the lists of Zonal Council members.
days.pyq: PYQs on the federal character of the Constitution, the Inter-State Council, Zonal Councils and water disputes, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Check what each body rests on. The Inter-State Council comes from a constitutional provision (Art 263) and was set up by a Presidential order in 1990. Zonal Councils are statutory, under the States Reorganisation Act 1956. UPSC often asks you to sort bodies this way.

days.task:
'Centre-State Relations' in three parts:
- Legislative: the Seventh Schedule, residuary powers, Arts 249, 250, 252 and 253, and reservation of state bills (Arts 200-201).
- Administrative: Arts 256-257, the All-India Services and Art 355.
- Financial: how taxes are distributed, and grants under Arts 275 and 282.
Skim the Sarkaria and Punchhi Commission recommendations.
days.pyq: PYQs on residuary powers, Arts 249/252/253, grants-in-aid and Seventh Schedule subjects, 2013-2026.
days.tip: UPSC often frames questions as 'Parliament can legislate on a State List subject when...'. Memorise the five situations (Art 249, national emergency, Art 252, Art 253, President's Rule) and the voting requirement for each.

days.task:
'Emergency Provisions':
- National Emergency (Art 352): grounds; approval within one month by special majority; changes made by the 44th Amendment; effect on FRs (Art 358 vs Art 359, and Arts 20-21 cannot be suspended).
- President's Rule (Art 356): approval within two months by simple majority, a maximum of 3 years, and the S.R. Bommai limits.
- Financial Emergency (Art 360).
days.pyq: PYQs on Arts 352/356/360 and the 44th Amendment safeguards, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Make one comparison table with the rows: grounds / approval period / majority / maximum duration / revocation (including the Lok Sabha resolution to revoke) / effect on FRs. Almost every emergency question can be answered from it.

days.task:
'President':
- election: electoral college, value of votes, disputes go to the Supreme Court
- qualifications, and impeachment under Art 61
- powers: executive, legislative, financial, judicial (types of pardon under Art 72), diplomatic, military and emergency
- veto powers (absolute, suspensive, pocket) and ordinance-making (Art 123)
- constitutional position after the 42nd and 44th Amendments
days.pyq: PYQs on the President's election, veto, ordinances, pardon and discretion, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Keep track of who votes where. Nominated MPs take part in impeaching the President but not in electing him. MLCs never vote in either. In the Vice-President's election all MPs vote, including nominated ones, and MLAs do not.

days.task: 'Vice-President': election, and removal by a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha; role as Rajya Sabha Chairman. Then 'Prime Minister' and 'Central Council of Ministers': Arts 74-75, the 15% cap from the 91st Amendment, collective versus individual responsibility, the kitchen cabinet. Skim 'Cabinet Committees' for names only and which ones the PM chairs.
days.pyq: PYQs on the Vice-President, collective responsibility, the size of the Council of Ministers and cabinet committees, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Under Art 75(3) the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha only. A non-member can be a minister for up to six months. The word 'Cabinet' entered the Constitution only through the 44th Amendment, in Art 352.

days.task:
(14 Nov, tough chapters in the 3h slot) 'Parliament' in full:
- organisation; composition and duration of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha; women's reservation (106th Amendment, 2023)
- membership and disqualification: Art 102 and the Tenth Schedule
- presiding officers: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, panel of chairpersons, pro-tem Speaker
- sessions: summoning, adjournment, prorogation, dissolution, and which bills lapse
- devices: question hour, zero hour, motions
- legislative procedure: ordinary, money and financial bills; joint sitting (Art 108)
- budget: stages, cut motions, appropriation, vote on account, guillotine, the three funds
- special powers and position of the Rajya Sabha
Then 'Parliamentary Committees': PAC, Estimates, COPU and the DRSCs, with composition and chair. Skim 'Parliamentary Forums' and 'Parliamentary Group'. The Parliament chapter is the longest in the book; if it eats the full 3h, move Parliamentary Committees to Sunday's backlog slot rather than rushing it.
days.pyq: 2h block: all Parliament PYQs from 2013-2026 (the second-biggest pool). Then write short-note tables: Lok Sabha vs Rajya Sabha, Money Bill vs Financial Bill, and the three financial committees.
days.tip: These questions turn on single facts. The Speaker certifies a money bill. There is no joint sitting for money bills or Constitution amendment bills. The PAC chairman comes from the Opposition by convention. The Estimates Committee has no Rajya Sabha members. Know which bills lapse when the Lok Sabha is dissolved.

days.task: 9:30-11:30 test on the Week 2 portion (Federal System through Parliament), plus 10 questions from Week 1. Then the mistake log. Revise the Emergency table, the President's powers and the Parliament tables. Do a quick pass over the Week 1 FR/DPSP sheet. Clear any backlog, such as Parliamentary Committees (if carried over) and the Parliamentary Forums skim.
days.pyq: Re-attempt the Week 2 PYQs you got wrong, and redo the Week 1 FR PYQs you marked as guesses.
days.tip: This is your 7-day spaced revision of Week 1. Revise it only from your one-page notes, not from Laxmikanth. That shows you whether the notes can stand on their own for later revisions.

weeks.theme: Judiciary, State Government, Local Government, UTs and Special Areas, Constitutional and Non-constitutional Bodies

days.task: 'Supreme Court': composition; appointment and the collegium (Second and Third Judges cases; NJAC struck down in 2015); removal; jurisdiction (original under Art 131, writ under Art 32, appellate, advisory under Art 143); court of record; power of judicial review. Then 'Judicial Review': Arts 13, 32 and 226, the Ninth Schedule and the I.R. Coelho case. Skim 'Judicial Activism' and 'Public Interest Litigation' for the meaning and the relaxed locus standi only.
days.pyq: PYQs on Supreme Court jurisdiction, advisory jurisdiction, the collegium, judicial review and PIL, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Know which jurisdiction a dispute falls under. Centre-State disputes go to original jurisdiction (Art 131), which excludes pre-Constitution treaties, and Art 262 lets Parliament bar courts from water disputes. An advisory opinion under Art 143 does not bind the President.

days.task: 'Governor': appointment by the President (not elected) and office during the President's pleasure; reservation of bills (Art 200), ordinances (Art 213), pardon (Art 161 vs Art 72); constitutional versus situational discretion. Then 'Chief Minister' and 'State Council of Ministers', reading only how they differ from the PM and Union Council of Ministers chapters.
days.pyq: PYQs on the Governor's discretion, Arts 200/201 and the pardon comparison with the President, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Draw a President vs Governor table covering pardon (the Governor cannot pardon a court-martial sentence), ordinances, veto and emergency roles. UPSC prefers comparative statements to isolated facts.

days.task: 'State Legislature', only where it differs from Parliament: creating and abolishing Legislative Councils (Art 169), the Council's weaker position, and the fact that the Council can only delay an ordinary bill. Then 'High Court': Arts 214-231, appointment, transfer and jurisdiction. Skim 'Subordinate Courts', mainly the appointment of district judges (Art 233). Read 'Tribunals' (Arts 323A and 323B).
days.pyq: PYQs on Legislative Councils, High Court jurisdiction and tribunals, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Classic trap: High Court writ jurisdiction under Art 226 is wider than the Supreme Court's under Art 32, because it covers 'any other purpose' (legal rights too). But Art 32 is itself a Fundamental Right and Art 226 is not.

days.task: 'Panchayati Raj': Balwant Rai Mehta → Ashok Mehta → 73rd Amendment; compulsory versus voluntary provisions; the 29 subjects of the Eleventh Schedule; State Election Commission and State Finance Commission; PESA 1996. Then 'Municipalities': the 74th Amendment, types of urban bodies, the 18 subjects of the Twelfth Schedule, District and Metropolitan Planning Committees. Skim 'Co-operative Societies': the 97th Amendment, Art 19(1)(c), Art 43B and Part IXB (note that in 2021 the Supreme Court struck down Part IXB as far as it applies to state co-operative societies; it survives for multi-state ones).
days.pyq: PYQs on the 73rd and 74th Amendments, PESA and the Gram Sabha, 2013-2026.
days.tip: Sort the provisions into two lists. Compulsory: three tiers (a state with population not exceeding 20 lakh may skip the intermediate tier), 5-year term, SC/ST reservation, one-third seats for women, SEC, SFC. Voluntary: OBC reservation, voting rights for MPs and MLAs, financial powers. Most panchayat questions test this split.

days.task: 'Union Territories': Arts 239-241, Delhi under Art 239AA, Puducherry, the administrator, and the 2019 reorganisation of J&K and Ladakh. 'Scheduled and Tribal Areas': Fifth versus Sixth Schedule, autonomous district councils, the Governor's role. 'Special Provisions for Some States' (Arts 371-371J): skim the state-wise list. Skim the J&K chapter (post-2019).
days.pyq: PYQs on the Fifth and Sixth Schedules, governance of Delhi and Art 371, 2013-2026.
days.tip: The Sixth Schedule covers only Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Fifth Schedule areas are declared by the President. Expect statement questions that swap the two.

days.task:
(21 Nov, 3h slot)
First 2h 15m, constitutional bodies: 'Election Commission', 'Union Public Service Commission', 'State Public Service Commission', 'Finance Commission', 'Goods and Services Tax Council', 'National Commission for SCs', 'National Commission for STs', 'National Commission for Backward Classes', 'Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities', 'Comptroller and Auditor General of India', 'Attorney General of India' and 'Advocate General of the State'.
Last 45 min, non-constitutional bodies: 'NITI Aayog', 'National Human Rights Commission', 'Central Information Commission', 'Central Vigilance Commission', 'Central Bureau of Investigation' and 'Lokpal and Lokayuktas'. For these, read only composition, appointment, removal and term.
days.pyq: 2h block: PYQs on the CAG, Attorney General, Election Commission, Finance Commission, NHRC, CIC, Lokpal and NITI Aayog, 2013-2026. Then build a master bodies table with the columns Article/Act | Composition | Appointed by | Removal | Term | Reports to.
days.tip: UPSC keeps asking two things: is the body constitutional or statutory, and who can remove its head. For example, the CAG is removed the same way as a Supreme Court judge. The Attorney General holds office at the President's pleasure and can speak in Parliament but cannot vote.

days.task: 9:30-11:30: test on the Week 3 portion plus 20 mixed questions from Weeks 1-2, as a mini-mock on the whole of Polity. Then the mistake log. In the afternoon, skim the remaining low-yield chapters: 'Official Language', 'Public Services', 'Rights and Liabilities of the Government', 'Special Provisions relating to Certain Classes' (SC/ST seat reservation in legislatures; the 104th Amendment ended Anglo-Indian nomination), 'Anti-Defection Law' (re-read it with the Tenth Schedule), and 'Elections' and 'Electoral Reforms' (EVM, VVPAT and NOTA basics only). Skim or skip the rest of the Political Dynamics part, the 'National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution' chapter and the appendices. Revise the one-page notes from all three weeks.
days.pyq: Across the whole book, re-attempt only the PYQs you got wrong or guessed. Note which Polity themes repeat across years.
days.tip: Polity now moves into your revision cycle. Revise the one-page notes on Day 7, Day 30 and Day 60, using the Sunday revision slots. Aim for 85%+ accuracy on Polity PYQs, because it is the highest-scoring static subject.

howToStudy: PYQs first. Before you open a Laxmikanth chapter, spend 10 minutes reading its 2013-2026 PYQs so you only underline what UPSC actually tests. After reading the chapter, solve those PYQs properly with a timer.

Read for the procedural details: who appoints, how the person is removed, what majority is needed, the time limits (14 days, 1 month, 2 months, 6 months) and which House acts. These details decide most Polity statements.

Make comparison tables instead of paragraph notes: FR vs DPSP vs FD, Lok Sabha vs Rajya Sabha, President vs Governor, Art 352 vs 356 vs 360, Supreme Court vs High Court writs, and constitutional vs statutory vs executive bodies. Keep it to one page per chapter.
Underline absolute words in statements, such as 'only', 'must', 'all', 'cannot' and 'directly enforceable'. Most of UPSC's Polity traps are a correct fact with one word changed.

Learn landmark cases by the principle they set, not by their facts: Kesavananda (basic structure), Minerva Mills (balance between FRs and DPSPs), S.R. Bommai (limits on Art 356), Maneka Gandhi (Art 21 procedure must be fair, just and reasonable), Puttaswamy (privacy), Indra Sawhney (50% ceiling, creamy layer).

Do not memorise every Article number. Learn only the high-yield ones (12-35, 51A, 72, 110, 123, 143, 148, 280, 312, 324, 352, 356, 360, 368). During your commute, link Polity news (bills, Supreme Court judgments, appointments) back to the right chapter.

Skim the Political Dynamics chapters and the appendices; do not study them. Revise from your own notes, not the book. A full Laxmikanth revision from notes should take about 3 hours. Revise on Day 7, Day 30, Day 60 and again in the last 6 weeks before Prelims.
blocks.scope: Laxmikanth Indian Polity: constitutional framework, FRs/DPSP/FDs, Parliament, Executive, Judiciary, Federalism, Local govt, bodies, Emergency, Amendments

blocks.name: Modern History + Art & Culture

weeks.theme: Modern India I (Spectrum): Europeans, British expansion, resistance, 1857, socio-religious reform, education and press

days.task: 23 Nov. Spectrum: skim 'Sources for the History of Modern India' and 'Major Approaches to the History of Modern India' (15 min, low-yield). Then read 'Advent of the Europeans in India' in full: Portuguese (Almeida, Albuquerque), Dutch, English (factories, Surat, Madras, Bombay, Calcutta), French, Danes, Anglo-French rivalry and the three Carnatic Wars.
days.pyq: Modern History PYQs on European trading companies, factories and Carnatic Wars, 2011-2025
days.tip: Make one table: company, first factory, key governor, main rival. UPSC asks which power held which settlement, not battle narratives.

days.task: 24 Nov. Spectrum: 'India on the Eve of British Conquest' (Mughal decline and successor states such as Hyderabad, Awadh, Bengal, Mysore and the Marathas; skim the socio-economic sections in 10 min). Then 'Expansion and Consolidation of British Power in India', part 1: Plassey, Buxar, Treaty of Allahabad and Dual Government in Bengal, Anglo-Mysore Wars. This is a heavy night: read Plassey to Allahabad first. If the Mysore wars are left over, finish them in Wednesday's 15-min revision slot.
days.pyq: PYQs on Bengal Nawabs, Plassey/Buxar, Treaty of Allahabad, Mysore rulers, 2011-2025
days.tip: Note what each treaty gave the British (Diwani, territory, subsidiary troops). Treaty-to-outcome pairs are a common question format.

days.task: 25 Nov. Spectrum: 'Expansion and Consolidation of British Power in India', part 2: Anglo-Maratha Wars, Anglo-Sikh Wars and the annexation of Punjab, Sindh, Subsidiary Alliance (Wellesley), Doctrine of Lapse (Dalhousie). Skim relations with neighbours (Bhutan, Nepal, Burma, Afghanistan, Tibet). Keep the appendix list of Governors-General and Viceroys as a reference only. Do not read it end to end.
days.pyq: PYQs on Subsidiary Alliance, Doctrine of Lapse, Governors-General and their policies, 2011-2025
days.tip: Make a one-page 'Governor-General and signature policy' list. UPSC mixes up Wellesley, Dalhousie and Bentinck reforms in statement questions.

days.task: 26 Nov. Spectrum: 'People's Resistance Against British Before 1857': civil uprisings (Sanyasi-Fakir, Poligars, Velu Thampi, Paika), peasant movements with religious overtones (Wahabi, Kuka, Faraizi, Moplah), tribal revolts (Santhal, Kol, Bhil, Khasi, Ahom, Munda), sepoy mutinies before 1857.
days.pyq: PYQs on tribal and peasant uprisings (Santhal, Munda, Faraizi, Kuka, Paika), 2011-2025
days.tip: Map each revolt to region, leader and decade. UPSC regularly asks 'which of these were tribal revolts' or leader-revolt matching.

days.task: 27 Nov. Spectrum: 'The Revolt of 1857': causes, the spark (Enfield rifle), centres and leaders, British commanders who suppressed it, reasons for failure, Queen's Proclamation and Government of India Act 1858, nature of the revolt (historians' views: skim).
days.pyq: PYQs on 1857 leaders and centres, Queen's Proclamation, Act of 1858, 2011-2025
days.tip: Prepare a three-column chart: centre, Indian leader, British officer. Centre-leader matching is the most-asked format.

days.task: 28 Nov, 3h heavy reading (tough, high-yield). About 2h: Spectrum 'Socio-Religious Reform Movements: General Features' plus 'A General Survey of Socio-Cultural Reform Movements' (Brahmo Samaj, Prarthana Samaj, Young Bengal, Vidyasagar, Arya Samaj, Ramakrishna Mission, Theosophical Society, Aligarh Movement, Ahmadiyya, Sikh and Parsi reform, Satyashodhak Samaj, SNDP, Self-Respect Movement, women's and caste reform laws). About 1h, PYQ-focused: 'Development of Indian Press' (key papers and press laws) and 'Development of Education' (Charter Act 1813, Macaulay's Minute, Wood's Despatch, Hunter Commission, Sadler, Hartog, Wardha scheme). If press or education is left over, finish it in Sunday's backlog slot. Rest of day: 2h PYQs and short notes, 1.5h CSAT, 1h weekly current affairs.
days.pyq: Socio-religious reform, press and education PYQs, 2011-2025 (founder-organisation-newspaper questions)
days.tip: Make a founder, organisation, year, newspaper/book grid. UPSC asks reformer-publication pairs (for example Rammohan Roy and Mirat-ul-Akhbar) and which law came under which Governor-General.

days.task: 29 Nov. 9:30-11:30 weekly test (40-50 Qs): Advent of the Europeans through Socio-Cultural Reform Movements, Press and Education. Then mistake analysis (log each error as fact gap, misreading or elimination error), revise this week's short notes and Week 3 notes, clear backlog. Evening off.
days.pyq: Re-attempt only the PYQs you got wrong this week
days.tip: For every wrong answer, write the one deciding fact on a revision card. Re-read those cards before next Sunday's test.

weeks.theme: Modern India II (Spectrum): Rise of nationalism to Quit India and INA

days.task: 30 Nov. Spectrum: 'Beginning of Modern Nationalism in India' (skim pre-Congress associations, list only: Landholders' Society, British Indian Association, East India Association, Indian Association, Madras Mahajan Sabha, Poona Sarvajanik Sabha). Then 'Indian National Congress: Foundation and the Moderate Phase': safety-valve theory, Moderate leaders, economic critique and Drain Theory (Dadabhai Naoroji), Indian Councils Act 1892.
days.pyq: PYQs on pre-Congress associations, early INC, Drain Theory, Moderates' demands, 2011-2025
days.tip: UPSC asks which association was founded by whom and where. Learn the founder-city pairs, not the long background.

days.task: 1 Dec. Spectrum: 'Era of Militant Nationalism (1905-1909)': partition of Bengal, Swadeshi and Boycott, Lal-Bal-Pal, Surat split 1907, Morley-Minto Reforms 1909. Then 'First Phase of Revolutionary Activities (1907-1917)': Bengal (Anushilan, Jugantar, Alipore case), Maharashtra, Punjab, overseas (India House, Ghadar; skim details).
days.pyq: PYQs on Swadeshi Movement, Surat split, Morley-Minto Reforms, Ghadar Party, 2011-2025
days.tip: Note Swadeshi-era institutions (Bengal National College, Swadeshi stores) and Ghadar personalities. UPSC likes statements on 'methods used in the Swadeshi Movement'.

days.task: 2 Dec. Spectrum: 'First World War and Nationalist Response' (Home Rule Leagues of Tilak and Besant, Lucknow Pact 1916, Montagu's August Declaration 1917). Then 'Emergence of Gandhi' (South Africa, Champaran, Ahmedabad mill strike, Kheda, Rowlatt Satyagraha, Jallianwala Bagh, Hunter Committee).
days.pyq: PYQs on Home Rule League, Lucknow Pact, Champaran/Kheda, Rowlatt Act, 2011-2025
days.tip: For Gandhi's early satyagrahas, note the exact grievance (tinkathia, wage hike, revenue remission). UPSC writes statements that swap these grievances.

days.task: 3 Dec. Spectrum: 'Non-Cooperation Movement and Khilafat Aandolan' (Nagpur session programme, Chauri Chaura, withdrawal, Moplah). Then 'Emergence of Swarajists, Socialist Ideas, Revolutionary Activity and Other New Forces': focus on Swarajists vs No-changers, HRA/HSRA, Kakori, Bhagat Singh, Chittagong; skim youth, caste and peasant sub-sections.
days.pyq: PYQs on Non-Cooperation, Swaraj Party, HSRA, Kakori and Chittagong, 2011-2025
days.tip: UPSC tests whether you can separate NCM programme items (boycott of councils, courts, schools) from Civil Disobedience items (breaking salt law). Make a two-column comparison.

days.task: 4 Dec. Spectrum: 'Simon Commission and the Nehru Report' (Nehru Report recommendations, Jinnah's Fourteen Points). Then 'Civil Disobedience Movement and Round Table Conferences', part 1: Lahore session 1929 (Purna Swaraj), Dandi March, spread of CDM (Peshawar and Abdul Ghaffar Khan, Dharasana, North-East and Rani Gaidinliu), First RTC, Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
days.pyq: PYQs on Nehru Report, Purna Swaraj, Dandi March, Gandhi-Irwin Pact, 2011-2025
days.tip: Learn what the Gandhi-Irwin Pact did and did not grant. UPSC builds wrong statements on the omitted demands, such as an inquiry into police excesses.

days.task: 5 Dec, 3h heavy reading (about 60 pages, so skim where marked). Spectrum: finish 'Civil Disobedience Movement and Round Table Conferences' (Karachi session resolutions, 2nd and 3rd RTC, Communal Award, Poona Pact). 'Debates on the Future Strategy after Civil Disobedience Movement' (10-min skim). 'Congress Rule in Provinces' (10-min skim, note the 1937 elections and work of the ministries). 'Nationalist Response in the Wake of World War II' (August Offer, Individual Satyagraha, Cripps Mission). 'Quit India Movement, Demand for Pakistan, and the INA' (Quit India resolution, parallel governments of Ballia, Tamluk and Satara, C.R. Formula, Desai-Liaqat, Wavell Plan, Simla Conference, INA). Rest of day: 2h PYQs and short notes, 1.5h CSAT, 1h weekly current affairs.
days.pyq: PYQs on Karachi resolution, Poona Pact, Cripps Mission, Quit India, INA, 2011-2025
days.tip: Make a 'proposals' table (August Offer, Cripps, C.R. Formula, Wavell Plan): year, key offer, why rejected. Comparing these plans is a favourite UPSC theme.

days.task: 6 Dec. 9:30-11:30 weekly test (40-50 Qs): Beginning of Modern Nationalism through Quit India/INA. Mistake analysis, then revise Week 5 and Week 4 short notes (reform movements grid and 1857 chart). Clear backlog. Evening off.
days.pyq: Redo wrong PYQs from Weeks 4 and 5
days.tip: Draw one timeline from 1885 to 1945 on a single sheet with sessions, acts and movements. Chronology-ordering questions become easy once this sheet is memorised.

weeks.theme: Modern India III (Spectrum thematic chapters) and selected Art and Culture (Nitin Singhania)

days.task: 7 Dec. Spectrum: 'Post-War National Scenario' (INA trials, RIN revolt 1946, 1945-46 elections, Cabinet Mission plan). Then 'Independence with Partition' (Direct Action Day, Attlee's statement, Mountbatten Plan, Indian Independence Act 1947, integration of princely states: skim).
days.pyq: PYQs on Cabinet Mission, RIN mutiny, Mountbatten Plan, Indian Independence Act, 2011-2025
days.tip: Cabinet Mission provisions (groupings A/B/C, Constituent Assembly method) are asked often. Memorise its structure and how it differs from Cripps.

days.task: 8 Dec. Spectrum: 'Constitutional, Administrative and Judicial Developments', Acts first (Regulating Act 1773, Pitt's India Act, Charter Acts 1793/1813/1833/1853, Acts of 1858, 1861, 1892, 1909, 1919, 1935), then civil services, police and judiciary under Cornwallis and Bentinck. Skim 'Survey of British Policies in India' (princely states, frontier policy) only if time is left; otherwise move it to Sunday's backlog slot.
days.pyq: PYQs on Charter Acts, GoI Acts 1919/1935, civil services and judicial reforms, 2011-2025
days.tip: Make a single 'Act, Governor-General, three key provisions' table. Revise it alongside Laxmikanth's 'Historical Background' chapter, since Polity and History overlap here.

days.task: 9 Dec. Spectrum: 'Economic Impact of British Rule in India' (deindustrialisation, Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari, Mahalwari, commercialisation of agriculture, famines, drain of wealth). 'Peasant Movements 1857-1947' (Indigo revolt, Pabna, Deccan riots, Kisan Sabhas, Eka, Moplah, Bardoli, AIKS, Tebhaga, Telangana). 'The Movement of the Working Class': 5-min skim for AITUC 1920, Trade Unions Act 1926 and the Meerut conspiracy case only. Priority order if short of time: land revenue systems, then peasant movements, then the rest.
days.pyq: PYQs on land revenue systems, peasant movements, AITUC, 2011-2025
days.tip: Land revenue systems and peasant revolts are UPSC favourites. Note region, year and who settled each one (Cornwallis, Munro and Read, Holt Mackenzie). Modern History is now complete; Sunday covers it all.

days.task: 10 Dec. Nitin Singhania, 'Indian Architecture, Sculpture and Pottery', part 1 (early India only): Harappan art (skim), Mauryan pillars, stupas and caves (Barabar), post-Mauryan Buddhist and Jain architecture (stupa, chaitya, vihara; Sanchi, Bharhut), schools of sculpture (Gandhara, Mathura, Amaravati), rock-cut caves (Ajanta, Ellora, Elephanta, Udayagiri-Khandagiri). Skip pottery. Read Indo-Islamic and modern architecture from PYQs only.
days.pyq: Art and Culture PYQs on stupas, cave sites and sculpture schools, 2013-2025
days.tip: UPSC asks for features, not dates: the material of each sculpture school, Buddhist vs Jain vs Hindu cave sites, and the parts of a stupa (anda, harmika, chhatra, torana). Make one comparison table.

days.task: 11 Dec. Nitin Singhania, 'Indian Paintings': prehistoric (Bhimbetka, skim), murals (Ajanta, Bagh, Sittanavasal), Pala and Apabhramsa miniatures, Mughal painting (Akbar to Jahangir), Rajasthani schools (Mewar, Kishangarh, Bundi-Kota), Pahari schools (Basohli, Kangra), Deccan schools. Skim modern painting and folk paintings (Madhubani, Pattachitra, Warli, Kalamkari, Phad) as one-line notes.
days.pyq: PYQs on miniature schools, mural sites, folk paintings and their states, 2013-2025
days.tip: Folk painting-to-state and school-to-theme pairs (Kishangarh and Bani Thani, Kangra and Gita Govinda themes) are the commonest format. Keep a one-page map list.

days.task: 12 Dec, 3h heavy reading. About 1h15: Singhania 'Indian Architecture, Sculpture and Pottery', part 2, temple architecture: Nagara (Odisha, Khajuraho, Solanki and Dilwara), Dravida (Pallava, Chola, Vijayanagara, Nayaka), Vesara (Chalukya, Hoysala). About 45 min: 'Indian Dance Forms' (the eight classical dances: origin state, patron/reviver, distinctive features; skim folk dances). About 30 min: 'Indian Music' (Hindustani vs Carnatic, Dhrupad, Khayal, Thumri, Carnatic trinity, Purandara Dasa; skim gharanas). About 30 min: Bhakti and Sufi movements (Alvars and Nayanars, Virashaiva, Ramananda, Kabir, Nanak, Chaitanya, Sankaradeva, Mirabai, Tukaram; Chishti, Suhrawardi, Naqshbandi orders), using the Bhakti-Sufi pages of Singhania (check your edition's contents). Rest of day: 2h PYQs and short notes, 1.5h CSAT, 1h weekly current affairs.
days.pyq: PYQs on temple styles, classical dances, music forms, Bhakti-Sufi saints, 2013-2025
days.tip: Use matching lists: temple-dynasty-style, dance-state-reviver, saint-region-language/text, Sufi order-founder-centre. Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises eight classical dances, and the Ministry of Culture also counts Chhau, so read the question's wording carefully.

days.task: 13 Dec. 9:30-11:30 test: full Modern History mini-mock (Spectrum, all chapters) plus Art and Culture covered Thu-Sat. Mistake analysis, then 20 min reading Singhania's 'UNESCO's List of World Heritage Sites in India' and 'UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage' as lists only (check the latest additions in current affairs, because the book lists go out of date). Revise Week 6 notes and the Week 5 timeline sheet. Clear any Spectrum backlog before the next subject block begins. Evening off.
days.pyq: Mixed Modern History and Art and Culture PYQ set (50 Qs, untimed), focusing on topics missed in the mock
days.tip: Tag every Modern History mistake as chronology, personality or provision. That tells you which of your three revision sheets to reread before the next cycle.

howToStudy: Read Spectrum PYQ-first. Before each chapter, glance at its last 10 years of PYQs so you know which details to underline: organisations, founders, acts, sessions and leaders. Skip historiography and long appendices, but keep the Governors-General list as a reference.

Build three master sheets and revise only these on weekdays: (1) a timeline from 1757 to 1947 with acts, sessions and movements, (2) a personality grid (person, organisation, newspaper/book, movement), (3) an acts table (Act, Governor-General, key provisions). A large share of Modern History MCQs can be answered from these three.

UPSC frames Modern History as statement elimination. While reading, note what a movement or plan did NOT include. For example, the Gandhi-Irwin Pact had no inquiry into police excesses, and the 1919 Act did not give provincial autonomy. Wrong statements are built from these gaps.

Treat Art and Culture as a matching subject. Keep compact tables (temple-dynasty-style, sculpture school-material-patron, dance-state-features, painting school-theme, Sufi order-founder-centre). Use Singhania only for the chapters UPSC has repeatedly asked from. Questions are mostly matching or 'how many pairs are correct'.

Art and Culture questions are often triggered by the news: new UNESCO inscriptions, GI tags, anniversaries of saints or reformers. When such an item appears in your commute reading, add one line to the matching Art and Culture table that weekend.

Link History and Polity. Revise the Charter Acts, the 1909/1919/1935 Acts and the Cabinet Mission together with Laxmikanth's 'Historical Background' and 'Making of the Constitution' chapters, so you prepare them once for both subjects.

Keep the commute for current affairs. Do your 5-minute master-sheet recall in the nightly 15-minute revision slot and again before each Sunday test. In every test, log each error as a fact gap, misreading or over-elimination, and re-read only the deciding facts, not whole chapters.
blocks.scope: Spectrum Modern India + selected Art & Culture

blocks.name: Geography

weeks.theme: Geomorphology: origin, interior, plate tectonics, rocks, geomorphic processes and landforms (NCERT Class 11 Fundamentals of Physical Geography, first half)

days.task: 14 Dec. 15 min: revise the previous night's notes. 75 min reading: skim 'Geography as a Discipline' . Then read all of 'The Origin and Evolution of the Earth': the nebular and Big Bang theories, the formation of stars and planets, the Moon, and the evolution of the lithosphere, atmosphere and hydrosphere. Atlas : world physical map. Mark the continents, the major fold mountains (Andes, Rockies, Alps, Himalayas, Atlas, Urals) and the major plateaus.
days.pyq: Geography PYQs (2011-2026) on the solar system, the Earth's origin, the evolution of the atmosphere and the geological time scale. Do about 10, then write down why each wrong option is wrong.
days.tip: UPSC rarely asks the theories themselves. It asks the order of events. NCERT gives three stages for the atmosphere: (1) the primordial atmosphere is lost to solar winds, (2) degassing from the hot interior (degassing and outgassing are the same thing), and (3) photosynthesis by living things adds oxygen. Make a one-line timeline instead of prose notes.

days.task: 15 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: 'Interior of the Earth'. Cover the direct and indirect sources, earthquake waves (P, S and surface waves), shadow zones, the types of earthquakes and how they are measured (Richter magnitude and Mercalli intensity), the structure of the Earth (crust, mantle, core, and the Moho and Gutenberg discontinuities), volcanoes (shield, composite, caldera, flood basalt provinces, mid-ocean ridge) and intrusive forms (batholith, laccolith, lapolith, phacolith, sill, dyke). Atlas: the Pacific Ring of Fire, the Deccan Traps and Barren Island.
days.pyq: Geography PYQs (2011-2026) on earthquake waves, shadow zones, volcanic landforms and the Ring of Fire.
days.tip: Draw the shadow-zone diagram once from memory. P-waves are absent only between 105 and 145 degrees, while S-waves are absent everywhere beyond 105 degrees. Statement traps usually swap these values.

days.task: 16 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: 'Distribution of Oceans and Continents'. Cover Wegener's continental drift and its evidence, the post-drift studies (convection currents and ocean-floor mapping), sea-floor spreading, plate tectonics (divergent, convergent and transform boundaries), the rates of plate movement and the movement of the Indian plate. Atlas: the major and minor plates, the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, the East African Rift, the San Andreas Fault and the Mariana Trench.
days.pyq: Geography PYQs (2011-2026) on plate tectonics, sea-floor spreading, mid-ocean ridges, trenches and the formation of the Himalayas.
days.tip: Learn a three-column table of boundary type, landform and example. UPSC tests matching between the three.

days.task: 17 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: skim 'Minerals and Rocks' in 25 min. This chapter is only in older editions and was dropped from the rationalised NCERT. Cover only the rock cycle, the three rock types with examples, and the metamorphic changes (limestone to marble, shale to slate, granite to gneiss). Then the first half of 'Geomorphic Processes': endogenic vs exogenic forces, diastrophism, weathering (chemical, physical, biological) and why it matters, and mass movements (slow ones such as creep and solifluction, rapid ones such as mudflow and debris avalanche, and landslides such as slump, rockslide and rockfall). Atlas: the landslide-prone belts of India (Western Ghats, Himalayas, North-East).
days.pyq: Geography PYQs (2011-2026) on rock types and examples, weathering and landslides.
days.tip: In weathering questions, link the climate to the process. Chemical weathering dominates in hot, humid climates. Physical weathering dominates in arid and cold climates: exfoliation in hot deserts and frost wedging in cold regions.

days.task: 18 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: the second half of 'Geomorphic Processes', covering erosion and deposition and soil formation (the process, and the five factors: parent material, topography, climate, biological activity and time). Then start 'Landforms and their Evolution' with the running-water section only: V-valleys, gorges, canyons, potholes, meanders, oxbow lakes, alluvial fans, deltas, levees and floodplains. Atlas: the Indian deltas (Ganga-Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) and estuaries (Narmada, Tapi).
days.pyq: Geography PYQs (2011-2026) on fluvial landforms, deltas vs estuaries and the factors of soil formation.
days.tip: Label every landform as erosional or depositional and give its stage (youth, mature or old). Statement questions often place a landform in the wrong category or stage.

days.task: 19 Dec. 3 h heavy reading: the rest of 'Landforms and their Evolution'. Cover groundwater/karst (sinkholes, lapies, stalactites, stalagmites), glaciers (cirque, horn, arete, U-shaped valley, fjord, moraines, eskers, drumlins, outwash plains), waves and currents (cliffs, sea caves, stacks, bars, spits, lagoons) and winds (pediments, playas, mushroom rocks, barchans, seifs). Then 2 h: PYQs and one-page short notes for the whole week, with a sketch for each group of landforms. Then 1.5 h CSAT and 1 h of weekly current affairs. Atlas: the Thar, Sahara, Gobi and Atacama deserts, the Norwegian fjords and the Sundarbans.
days.pyq: All landform PYQs (2011-2026): glacial, karst, coastal and aeolian. Also redo the Mon-Fri questions under a timer.
days.tip: Make one sheet with five columns (running water, groundwater, glacier, waves, wind) and two rows (erosional, depositional). UPSC pair-matching questions on landforms come straight from this grid.

days.task: 20 Dec. 9:30-11:30 AM: weekly test on geomorphology, covering the Earth's origin, the interior, plate tectonics, rocks, geomorphic processes and landforms (about 50 MCQs, including the pending atlas items). Afterwards: mistake analysis in the error notebook, revision of this week's notes and the Week 6 short notes, and any backlog. Evening off.
days.pyq: Redo every geomorphology PYQ you got wrong this week, without notes.
days.tip: Classify each mistake as a concept gap, a fact gap, or a misread or extreme word. If misreads are more than 20% of your mistakes, slow down on the statement stems.

weeks.theme: Climatology, oceanography and biogeography (NCERT Class 11 Fundamentals of Physical Geography, second half)

days.task: 21 Dec. 15 min: revise the landform grid. 75 min: 'Composition and Structure of Atmosphere' (gases, water vapour, dust; troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere, exosphere). Then 'Solar Radiation, Heat Balance and Temperature': insolation and why it varies, heating and cooling of the atmosphere (conduction, convection, advection), terrestrial radiation, the heat budget, albedo, the factors controlling temperature, isotherms and temperature inversion. Atlas: the January and July isotherm maps.
days.pyq: Geography PYQs (2011-2026) on the atmospheric layers, ozone, the heat budget, albedo and temperature inversion.
days.tip: UPSC likes 'why' questions, such as why the troposphere is thickest at the equator or why the highest temperatures are found in the subtropical deserts rather than at the equator. Write each reason in one line.

days.task: 22 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: the first half of 'Atmospheric Circulation and Weather Systems'. Cover atmospheric pressure (vertical and horizontal distribution), the pressure belts, the forces affecting wind (pressure gradient, friction, Coriolis), the general circulation (Hadley, Ferrel and polar cells), its effect on the oceans (El Nino/ENSO), seasonal winds and local winds (land and sea breezes, mountain and valley winds). Atlas: draw the global pressure belts and planetary winds on a blank world map.
days.pyq: Geography PYQs (2011-2026) on pressure belts, the Coriolis force, El Nino and La Nina, jet streams and local winds (Loo, Chinook, Foehn, Mistral, Harmattan).
days.tip: Practise drawing the three-cell model with the pressure belts until it takes you 2 minutes. Many climatology statement questions can be answered from this diagram.

days.task: 23 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: the second half of 'Atmospheric Circulation and Weather Systems'. Cover air masses, fronts (cold, warm, stationary, occluded), extratropical cyclones, tropical cyclones (the conditions for formation, the structure and eye, and the regional names: cyclones, hurricanes, typhoons, willy-willies), and thunderstorms and tornadoes. Atlas: the cyclone basins (Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, Caribbean, North-West Pacific) and the locations of the local winds.
days.pyq: Geography PYQs (2011-2026) on tropical vs temperate cyclones, the conditions for cyclone formation and fronts.
days.tip: Make a two-column comparison of tropical and extratropical cyclones (latitude of origin, energy source, fronts, direction of movement, size). It is a common source of statement questions.

days.task: 24 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: 'Water in the Atmosphere'. Cover humidity (absolute, relative, specific), evaporation and condensation, the forms of condensation (dew, frost, fog, mist), clouds (cirrus, cumulus, stratus, nimbus), the types of rainfall (convectional, orographic, cyclonic) and the world distribution of rainfall. Atlas: rain-shadow zones (the leeward side of the Western Ghats, Patagonia, Ladakh behind the Himalayas).
days.pyq: Geography PYQs (2011-2026) on humidity, dew point, cloud types, fog and smog, and the types of rainfall.
days.tip: Learn which variable changes in each process. For example, when air cools and its water content stays the same, its relative humidity rises. UPSC tests relationships like this one.

days.task: 25 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: 'Water (Oceans)'. Cover the hydrological cycle, the relief of the ocean floor (continental shelf, slope, deep-sea plain, trenches, ridges, seamounts, guyots, atolls) and the temperature and salinity of ocean water and how they are distributed. Then skim 'Life on the Earth' (older edition only) and 'Biodiversity and Conservation' in 20 min, because both are covered in depth later from Shankar IAS Environment. Atlas: the world's major trenches, plus the salinity extremes (Red Sea and Dead Sea high, Baltic Sea and Black Sea low).
days.pyq: Geography PYQs (2011-2026) on ocean-floor relief, salinity and its factors, and continental shelves.
days.tip: For salinity, learn what controls it. Evaporation and ice formation raise salinity. River inflow, rainfall and ice-melt lower it. Most 'highest or lowest salinity' options can then be worked out instead of memorised.

days.task: 26 Dec. 3 h heavy reading. First 'Movements of Ocean Water': waves; tides (spring, neap, perigee, apogee and why tides matter); and ocean currents (the forces behind them and the major warm and cold currents). Then 'World Climate and Climate Change': Koeppen's scheme (groups A, B, C, D, E and H with their key regions), past and present climate change, the greenhouse effect and the greenhouse gases. After that, 2 h of PYQs plus a one-page sheet for each chapter, and a world map of ocean currents (warm in red, cold in blue). Then 1.5 h CSAT and 1 h of current affairs. Atlas: the Gulf Stream, Kuroshio, Labrador, Canary, Benguela, Humboldt (Peru), West Australian and Agulhas currents, and the Grand Banks and other fishing grounds.
days.pyq: All PYQs (2011-2026) on ocean currents, tides, the Koeppen, Mediterranean and savanna climate regions, and the greenhouse effect.
days.tip: Learn the pattern. In low and middle latitudes, cold currents flow along the west coasts of continents, which is why coastal deserts such as the Atacama and Namib exist there. Major fishing grounds lie where warm and cold currents meet.

days.task: 27 Dec. 9:30-11:30 AM: weekly test on climatology and oceanography (atmosphere, insolation, pressure and winds, cyclones, humidity, oceans, currents, tides, Koeppen) plus about 10 recall questions on Week 7 geomorphology. Afterwards: mistake analysis, revision of the Week 8 and Week 7 short notes, and any backlog. Evening off.
days.pyq: Redo the climatology and oceanography PYQs you got wrong, then attempt the 10 hardest Week 7 PYQs again.
days.tip: Redraw the pressure belts and the ocean currents on blank maps from memory. Revise first whatever you cannot draw, before doing any more reading.

weeks.theme: India: Physical Environment (NCERT Class 11): location, physiography, drainage, soils, climate, natural vegetation and hazards

days.task: 28 Dec. 15 min: revise the currents map. 75 min: 'India - Location' (15 min: the latitude and longitude extent, the Standard Meridian at 82 degrees 30 minutes E, the neighbouring countries, and the Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar). Then the first half of 'Structure and Physiography'. Cover the geological divisions (the Peninsular Block, the Himalayas, the Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra plain) and the regional divisions of the Himalayas: Kashmir or North-western, Himachal and Uttarakhand, Darjeeling and Sikkim, Arunachal, and the Eastern hills and mountains (Patkai Bum, Naga, Mizo and Manipur hills). Atlas: the Karakoram, Ladakh, Zanskar and Pir Panjal ranges, and the passes Zoji La, Shipki La, Lipulekh, Nathu La and Bomdi La.
days.pyq: India geography PYQs (2011-2026) on the Himalayan ranges and passes, the states on the Tropic of Cancer and India's neighbours.
days.tip: UPSC asks for sequences, such as passes or hills from west to east, or the states the Tropic of Cancer crosses. Practise putting them in order on the atlas instead of only recognising the names.

days.task: 29 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: the second half of 'Structure and Physiography'. Cover the Northern Plains (bhabar, tarai, bhangar, khadar), the Peninsular Plateau (Deccan, Malwa, Chotanagpur and Meghalaya plateaus; the Western vs Eastern Ghats; peaks such as Anamudi and Doddabetta), the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains (western vs eastern) and the Islands (Andaman and Nicobar, and Lakshadweep). Atlas: the Ten, Nine and Eight Degree Channels, Barren Island, Narcondam, and the Aravalli, Vindhya, Satpura, Nilgiri and Cardamom hills.
days.pyq: India geography PYQs (2011-2026) on plateaus, hill ranges, peaks, coastal plains, and the islands and channels.
days.tip: Make a table comparing the Western and Eastern Ghats (continuity, height, rivers, rainfall, peaks). It is a frequent source of statement questions.

days.task: 30 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: the first half of 'Drainage System'. Cover the drainage patterns (dendritic, trellis, radial, centripetal), the drainage basins and the Himalayan rivers. These are the Indus system (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Satluj, Shyok, Gilgit), the Ganga system (Yamuna, Chambal, Betwa, Ken, Son, Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, Damodar) and the Brahmaputra system (Tsangpo, Dihang, Dibang, Lohit, Subansiri, Teesta). Atlas: trace each tributary from its source to where it joins the main river, and mark Devprayag, Prayagraj and the Kosi floodplain.
days.pyq: India geography PYQs (2011-2026) on the Himalayan rivers and their tributaries, sources and confluences, and on how the Himalayan drainage evolved.
days.tip: Draw a tributary tree for each system, with left-bank and right-bank tributaries on separate sides. UPSC asks which rivers are tributaries of X, and also which bank they join.

days.task: 31 Dec. 15 min revision. 75 min: the second half of 'Drainage System'. Cover the Peninsular rivers, both east-flowing (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Subarnarekha, Brahmani, Penner) and west-flowing (Narmada and Tapi in rift valleys, Mahi, Sabarmati, Periyar, Sharavati). Also cover the comparison of Himalayan and Peninsular rivers and river regimes. Atlas: the rivers in rift valleys, the Jog Falls (on the Sharavati), the Gulf of Khambhat, and the states each peninsular river flows through.
days.pyq: India geography PYQs (2011-2026) on the peninsular rivers, the west-flowing rivers, the order of states a river crosses, and waterfalls.
days.tip: Traps are built on the exceptions, so learn them. The Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys and form estuaries, not deltas. The Chambal, Betwa and Son rise in the peninsula but belong to the Ganga system.

days.task: 1 Jan. 15 min revision. 75 min: 'Soils', a chapter found only in older editions (dropped from the rationalised NCERT). Cover the classification and the alluvial, black, red and yellow, laterite, arid, saline, peaty and forest soils with their properties and regions, plus soil degradation, erosion and conservation. Then skim 'Natural Hazards and Disasters' in 20 min: the classification of hazards, earthquakes, tsunamis, tropical cyclones, floods, droughts and landslides. Disaster management comes later with GS3. Atlas: the black soil (Deccan) and laterite belts, and the seismic zones map of India. Use the latest BIS seismic zonation map (revised in 2025) as well as the NCERT map.
days.pyq: India geography PYQs (2011-2026) on soil types, their properties and the crops they suit, and on the seismic, flood and drought zones.
days.tip: For each soil, learn a three-part chain: parent rock and how it formed, its key chemical feature (rich or poor in what), and the crop it suits. UPSC statements usually test the middle part, for example that laterite is poor in nitrogen.

days.task: 2 Jan. 3 h heavy reading. First 'Climate' from India: Physical Environment. Cover the unity and diversity of the monsoon; the factors (latitude, the Himalayas, distribution of land and water, relief, air pressure and winds); the mechanism (shift of the ITCZ, jet streams, El Nino, the Tibetan plateau); the onset of the monsoon and breaks in it; the four seasons (including western disturbances, mango showers and Kalbaisakhi); the distribution of rainfall; and the Koeppen classification of India. Then 'Natural Vegetation': tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen, deciduous (moist and dry), tropical thorn, montane, and littoral and swamp (mangrove) forests, plus an outline of forest and wildlife conservation. After that, 2 h of PYQs and short notes, then 1.5 h CSAT and 1 h of current affairs. Atlas: the rainfall map of India, and national parks matched to vegetation type (Sundarbans, Silent Valley, Kaziranga, Gir, Desert NP, Hemis, Namdapha).
days.pyq: All PYQs (2011-2026) on the Indian monsoon, jet streams, western disturbances, the north-east monsoon and Tamil Nadu's rainfall, forest types, and where mangroves are found.
days.tip: Link rainfall to vegetation in one table, using the NCERT figures: more than 200 cm gives evergreen forest, 100-200 cm moist deciduous, 70-100 cm dry deciduous and under 50 cm thorn forest. UPSC mixes national parks with forest types, so add one national park example to each row.

days.task: 3 Jan. 9:30-11:30 AM: weekly test on India: Physical Environment (location, physiography, drainage, soils, climate, vegetation, hazards) plus about 15 cumulative questions from Weeks 7-8 and a 10-item blank-map drill (rivers, passes, national parks, straits). Afterwards: mistake analysis, revision of all three weeks' one-page sheets to close the geography block, and any backlog. Evening off.
days.pyq: Do a full timed set of India geography PYQs from the last 5 years, then redo every geography PYQ you got wrong in Weeks 7-9.
days.tip: Close the block with a 2-page geography master sheet holding the key diagrams and the exceptions list. Revise this sheet, not the NCERTs, in later revision cycles.

howToStudy: Do the map work every night. Find each river, pass, hill range, national park or strait you read about in the atlas the same night. UPSC asks for sequences (north to south, west to east), which states a river crosses, and which of several places lie in a region, so recognising names is not enough.

Learn the reason behind each fact. Physical geography statements test cause and effect, for example why subtropical west coasts have deserts, why the troposphere is thickest at the equator, or why the Narmada forms an estuary. Write the reason in one line next to the fact.

Draw diagrams instead of writing paragraphs. Your geography notes should be mostly drawings: the three-cell circulation, pressure belts, plate boundaries, the shadow zone, the ocean-currents map, tributary trees and the landform grid. A chapter is done when you can redraw them from memory.

Keep an exceptions list. UPSC traps sit in exceptions and extreme words. Examples: the Narmada and Tapi flow west, the Chambal and Son rise in the peninsula but belong to the Ganga system, the Tamil Nadu coast gets most of its rain in October-December from the north-east (retreating) monsoon, and laterite is poor in nitrogen. Read every 'only', 'all' and 'always' twice.

Read the PYQs first, then the NCERT. Before each chapter, spend 5 minutes on its PYQs to see how deep UPSC goes. India geography (rivers, soils, monsoon, vegetation) and world map work carry more weight than theories of origin.

Use one source. The NCERTs and an atlas are enough for static geography, so do not add a second book. Get extra depth from PYQ explanations and later from current affairs (cyclones, earthquakes, El Nino, glacial lakes, places in the news, revised maps such as the BIS seismic zones).

Make a 1-page sheet per chapter and keep an error notebook. Condense each chapter to one page when you finish it. In the Sunday mistake analysis, add every wrong fact to the exceptions list. In later revision cycles, revise these sheets, not the books.
blocks.scope: NCERT Class 11 Physical Geography + India Physical Environment + atlas

blocks.name: Economy

weeks.theme: Macro foundations: national income, money & banking, RBI tools, inflation, budget basics

days.task: NCERT Class 12 Macroeconomics Ch 1 'Introduction' (skim, 15 min: emergence of macroeconomics, the four sectors). Then Ch 2 'National Income Accounting' first half: stocks vs flows, circular flow of income, the three methods (Product/Value Added, Expenditure, Income) and why they give the same number.
days.pyq: Economy PYQs on national income concepts and GDP measurement, 2013-2026 (about 8-10 questions)
days.tip: UPSC asks about concepts, not derivations. Keep a 3-column note (method | what is added | what is excluded, e.g. intermediate goods, transfer payments, second-hand sales).

days.task: Ch 2 'National Income Accounting' second half: GDP, GNP, NNP at market price vs factor cost, net factor income from abroad, net indirect taxes, nominal vs real GDP, GDP deflator, CPI and WPI, GDP and welfare (externalities, non-monetary exchanges). Revise Monday's circular flow for 15 min.
days.pyq: PYQs on GDP vs GNP, GDP deflator and the CPI vs WPI basket, 2013-2026
days.tip: Make one formula card (GNP = GDP + NFIA; NNP = GNP - depreciation; NI = NNP at FC = NNP at MP - net indirect taxes). Almost every statement-based question here checks one of these signs.

days.task: Ch 3 'Money and Banking' first half: functions of money, barter, money supply measures M1, M2, M3, M4 and what each includes, legal tender vs fiat money, how commercial banks create money (balance sheet, reserve ratio, money multiplier).
days.pyq: PYQs on money supply measures, money multiplier and liquidity, 2013-2026
days.tip: Write the four definitions exactly: M1 = currency with public + demand deposits + other deposits with RBI; M2 = M1 + post office savings deposits; M3 = M1 + net time deposits of banks; M4 = M3 + total post office deposits. Note M3 is built on M1, not M2. A common trap is moving time deposits into M1.

days.task: Ch 3 second half: RBI as banker to government, lender of last resort and controller of credit. Then from your notes source: CRR, SLR, Repo, Reverse Repo, SDF, MSF, Bank Rate, OMO, LAF; quantitative vs qualitative tools; Monetary Policy Committee (set up through the 2016 amendment to the RBI Act, 6 members, Governor has a casting vote) and flexible inflation targeting (target notified by the Government every five years).
days.pyq: PYQs on RBI monetary policy tools, MPC and their effect on liquidity, 2013-2026
days.tip: For each tool, write which way it moves liquidity when raised. UPSC questions are of the form 'if RBI does X, what happens to Y'.

days.task: Topic: Inflation (notes source plus Ch 2 recap). Demand-pull vs cost-push, stagflation, deflation, disinflation, headline vs core inflation, CPI (Combined) vs WPI (who publishes, coverage, services), Phillips curve, effects of inflation on debtors and creditors, policy responses. Note the current base years of the GDP, CPI and WPI series from the latest MoSPI/DPIIT releases, as these series are being revised.
days.pyq: PYQs on inflation types, CPI/WPI and anti-inflation measures, 2013-2026
days.tip: UPSC asks 'who gains or loses from inflation' and 'which index includes services'. Keep a 2-column CPI vs WPI table (publisher, basket, services, use in inflation targeting) and you have most of this topic.

days.task: Heavy reading (3h). (a) Ch 4 'Determination of Income and Employment': aggregate demand, consumption function, MPC/MPS, investment multiplier, paradox of thrift, deficient and excess demand. Skim the algebra and keep only the ideas. (b) Ch 5 'Government Budget and the Economy' in full: objectives of the budget, revenue vs capital receipts and expenditure, revenue/fiscal/primary deficit, how deficits are financed, fiscal policy and the multiplier. Then 2h PYQs and short notes, 1.5h CSAT (quant: percentages, averages), 1h current-affairs consolidation (RBI policy, inflation prints).
days.pyq: Budget and deficit PYQs (revenue vs capital receipts, fiscal/primary deficit), 2013-2026; write short notes from the mistakes
days.tip: Classifying items (disinvestment, interest, grants, loan recovery) as revenue or capital is a favourite UPSC trap. Make a list of 15 items and classify them yourself.

days.task: 9:30-11:30 weekly test: Macro Ch 2-5, RBI tools, inflation (about 40 MCQs). Then mistake analysis, revise this week's formula and tool cards, clear any backlog, and revise last week's subject notes for 30 min.
days.pyq: Re-attempt every PYQ you got wrong this week, without looking at the answers
days.tip: Sort each mistake as concept gap, misread statement or guess. In Economy many errors come from careless reading of 'increase/decrease'.

weeks.theme: Fiscal policy, taxation and GST, external sector, banking, financial markets, international institutions

days.task: Topic: Fiscal policy and FRBM (notes source). FRBM Act 2003, its targets, the 2018 amendment (debt as the main anchor, fiscal deficit as operational target), escape clause, N.K. Singh Committee. Finance Commission (Art 280) and devolution. Consolidated Fund (Art 266), Contingency Fund (Art 267) and Public Account (Art 266(2)) (link to Laxmikanth). Outcome vs performance budgeting, zero-based budgeting.
days.pyq: PYQs on FRBM, Finance Commission, Consolidated/Contingency Fund and budget terms, 2013-2026
days.tip: Learn the three funds with their Article numbers and who controls withdrawals. UPSC mixes Polity and Economy facts in one question.

days.task: Topic: Taxation and GST. Direct vs indirect taxes, progressive/proportional/regressive, tax buoyancy vs elasticity. GST: 101st Amendment (2016), Art 246A, 269A (IGST) and 279A, GST Council composition and voting (Centre one-third weight, states two-thirds, decisions by three-fourths majority), CGST/SGST/IGST, destination principle, items outside GST (alcohol for human consumption; petroleum products until the Council recommends), input tax credit, GST compensation to states and the phasing out of the compensation cess.
days.pyq: PYQs on GST, tax types and the incidence of taxes, 2013-2026
days.tip: Keep to the constitutional and structural facts of GST. Rates and slabs change often (they were restructured in 2025), so do not memorise them for Prelims.

days.task: NCERT Ch 6 'Open Economy Macroeconomics' in full: balance of payments (current account: trade, invisibles, transfers; capital account: FDI, FPI, loans), BoP surplus and deficit, official reserve transactions, foreign exchange market, fixed vs flexible vs managed floating exchange rates, nominal and real exchange rate.
days.pyq: PYQs on BoP components and exchange-rate mechanisms, 2013-2026
days.tip: Practise placing items in the right account (remittances, FDI, ECB, software exports, NRI deposits). Most BoP questions UPSC sets come down to this.

days.task: Topic: External sector (notes source). FDI vs FPI, ECBs, masala bonds, current vs capital account convertibility, FEMA 1999 (it replaced FERA 1973), composition of forex reserves (FCA, gold, SDR, IMF reserve tranche), depreciation vs devaluation, NEER/REER, twin deficit, current account deficit and its financing.
days.pyq: PYQs on FDI/FPI, convertibility, forex reserves and rupee depreciation, 2013-2026
days.tip: For depreciation, write the effect on exports, imports, inflation and external debt servicing. UPSC asks this cause-and-effect chain often.

days.task: Topic: Banking (notes source). Structure: SCBs, RRBs, cooperative banks, payments banks, small finance banks, NBFCs. NPAs and asset classification, SARFAESI 2002, IBC 2016, ARCs, Basel norms (three pillars; capital adequacy under Basel III), priority sector lending, deposit insurance (DICGC), bank nationalisation (1969, 1980).
days.pyq: PYQs on bank types, NPAs/IBC, Basel norms and priority sector lending, 2013-2026
days.tip: Make a 'can / cannot' table for payments banks, small finance banks and NBFCs (lend? take demand deposits? issue credit cards?). This is a classic UPSC statement-question pattern.

days.task: Heavy reading (3h). (a) Financial markets: money market (call money, T-bills, CP, CD, repo market) vs capital market (equity, dated G-secs, corporate bonds), primary vs secondary market, regulators (SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA), mutual funds, REITs/InvITs, derivatives basics, ADR/GDR, P-notes; payment systems in brief (NPCI, UPI, RTGS/NEFT). (b) International economic institutions: IMF (quotas, SDR basket, lending), World Bank Group (IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID), WTO (MFN, national treatment, AoA amber/blue/green boxes, TRIPS, TRIMS, peace clause), BIS, AIIB, NDB, and which body publishes which report. Then 2h PYQs and short notes, 1.5h CSAT (reading comprehension), 1h current-affairs consolidation.
days.pyq: PYQs on money vs capital market instruments, IMF/World Bank/WTO and the reports they publish, 2013-2026
days.tip: Make an institution-to-report-to-headquarters table. Report and institution matching is asked frequently and is quick marks.

days.task: 9:30-11:30 weekly test: FRBM, GST/taxation, BoP and external sector, banking, financial markets, international institutions (about 40 MCQs). Then mistake analysis, revise this week's notes, and revise Week 10 cards (national income formulas, RBI tools, CPI vs WPI). Clear backlog.
days.pyq: Mixed re-attempt of wrong PYQs from Weeks 10-11
days.tip: If you keep confusing two terms (repo vs reverse repo, FDI vs FPI), write a one-line 'confusion pair' card for each and revise it daily next week.

weeks.theme: Indian Economic Development: planning, liberalisation, poverty, employment, agriculture, infrastructure, and Budget basics

days.task: NCERT Class 11 'Indian Economic Development' Ch 1 'Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence' (skim, 20 min: colonial agriculture, deindustrialisation, drain). Then Ch 2 'Indian Economy 1950-1990': goals of planning, Mahalanobis model, land reforms, Green Revolution, Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, small-scale industry, import substitution.
days.pyq: PYQs on Five Year Plans, land reforms, Green Revolution and IPR 1956, 2013-2026
days.tip: UPSC asks which plan or policy did what. Keep a one-page timeline: 1951 First Plan, 1956 IPR, 1969 bank nationalisation and MRTP Act, 1991 NEP, 2015 NITI Aayog.

days.task: IED Ch 3 'Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal': the 1991 BoP crisis, stabilisation vs structural reforms, industrial delicensing, financial and tax reforms, foreign exchange reforms, privatisation and disinvestment, Maharatna/Navratna, outsourcing, WTO, an appraisal of the reforms. Add the Planning Commission to NITI Aayog change (2015) from notes.
days.pyq: PYQs on 1991 reforms, disinvestment and PSU categories, 2013-2026
days.tip: Learn what 1991 actually changed (licensing abolished except for a short list, MRTP asset threshold removed, public-sector reserved industries cut sharply) versus what continued. Statement questions hinge on that line.

days.task: Poverty (not in the current rationalised IED; use the old-edition chapter 'Poverty' or your notes): absolute vs relative poverty, poverty line committees (Lakdawala, Tendulkar, Rangarajan), the NITI Aayog Multidimensional Poverty Index approach, anti-poverty programmes. Then IED Ch 6 'Employment: Growth, Informalisation and Other Issues': workers and employment, participation rates, self-employed vs regular vs casual, formal vs informal sector, types of unemployment (disguised, seasonal, structural), PLFS concepts.
days.pyq: PYQs on poverty estimation, unemployment types and labour-force terms, 2013-2026
days.tip: Learn exact definitions (labour force vs workforce, LFPR vs WPR vs unemployment rate). UPSC tests whether you can tell these ratios apart.

days.task: Topic: Agriculture. IED Ch 5 'Rural Development' (rural credit, NABARD, SHGs, cooperatives, agricultural marketing, diversification, organic farming), then notes: MSP and CACP, procurement, buffer stock, PDS and NFSA 2013, fertiliser and other input subsidies, APMC, crop insurance basics, land holdings pattern.
days.pyq: PYQs on MSP/CACP, PDS/food security, agri credit and marketing, 2013-2026
days.tip: Agriculture questions combine Economy and Geography. Note who recommends MSP (CACP), who approves it (CCEA), and that MSP has no statutory backing.

days.task: Topic: Infrastructure (not in the current rationalised IED; use the old-edition chapter 'Infrastructure' or notes): energy sources, power sector, transport, communication, project models (EPC, BOT, HAM), InvITs revisited. Then IED Ch 4 'Human Capital Formation in India' (skim, 15 min). IED Ch 7 'Environment and Sustainable Development' (skim, 10 min; the Environment block covers it in depth).
days.pyq: PYQs on infrastructure financing, PPP models and the energy sector, 2013-2026
days.tip: For project models, learn who finances and who bears the traffic/revenue risk in each (EPC: government funds and bears risk; BOT-toll: private party bears traffic risk; HAM: cost shared, government bears traffic risk). That is the usual point of difference in options.

days.task: Budget day (3h). Read a standard summary of Union Budget 2026-27 for structure: receipts and expenditure composition (rupee comes from / goes to), deficit indicators, capex push, major tax changes, flagship schemes. Skim only the concept boxes and new terms of Economic Survey 2025-26 (45 min max). Skim IED Ch 8 'Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours' . Note: Economic Survey 2026-27 and Budget 2027-28 are due around end-January / 1 Feb 2027, so schedule their summaries on the first two Saturdays of February in the current-affairs hour. Then 2h PYQs and short notes, 1.5h CSAT (data interpretation), 1h current-affairs consolidation.
days.pyq: PYQs where UPSC used Budget or Economic Survey themes (subsidies, capex, fiscal indicators, schemes), 2013-2026
days.tip: From the Budget and Survey, take only concepts and new schemes or terms, not exact figures. Prelims asks what a scheme does, not how much money it was given.

days.task: 9:30-11:30 cumulative Economy test covering all of Weeks 10-12 (about 50 MCQs mixing macro, fiscal, external, banking, IED). Then mistake analysis, a full revision of every Economy formula, table and confusion-pair card, and backlog clearance. Combine the short notes into one 15-20 page Economy revision booklet, leaving a blank page for the new Budget and Survey.
days.pyq: Full-length timed set of the last 5 years of Economy PYQs (2022-2026)
days.tip: The booklet is what you will revise in Feb-May. If a fact is not in it, assume you will not revise it, so make it complete now.

howToStudy: Start with concepts, then facts: UPSC Economy questions test whether you understand a mechanism (what happens to liquidity, exports or the deficit if X changes), so before memorising, write the cause-and-effect chain for every tool and indicator.

Classification is the core skill: practise sorting items into revenue vs capital, current vs capital account, money vs capital market and quantitative vs qualitative tools. Most statement questions are a hidden classification test.
Read PYQs before the chapter: spend 10 minutes on the topic's 2013-2026 PYQs before reading, so you read NCERT and your notes knowing exactly which lines get asked.
Learn structures and definitions, not numbers: skip exact rates, slabs and budget figures that change every year. Learn institutions, Articles, who chairs or recommends what, and formulas.

Keep tables and cards, not prose notes: a formula card, an RBI tools card, a BoP placement table, an institution-to-report table and 'confusion pair' cards (repo/reverse repo, FDI/FPI, CPI/WPI, M1/M3).
Read words like 'only', 'all', 'exclusively' and 'automatically' slowly. Economy statements are often wrong because of one absolute word or one swapped direction (increase/decrease).

Use current affairs only to support the static basics: on commutes, link every RBI policy or Budget news item back to the NCERT concept it tests, and add it to the relevant card instead of making separate notes.
blocks.scope: NCERT Macro & Indian Economic Development, inflation, RBI, fiscal policy, taxation, banking, external sector

blocks.name: Environment

weeks.theme: Environment I: Ecology, Ecosystems, Biodiversity and Protected Areas (Shankar IAS Units I-II), 25-31 Jan 2027

days.task: 25 Jan. Read the Shankar IAS chapter 'Ecology' (levels of organisation, habitat vs niche, ecotone and edge effect). Then read the first half of 'Functions of an Ecosystem' (food chain vs food web, trophic levels, ecological pyramids, the 10% law). Make a one-page note on the pyramid types and on when each one is inverted.
days.pyq: Environment PYQs 2013-2025 on ecology basics: ecotone, niche, food chains, pyramids and decomposers (about 10-12 questions).
days.tip: UPSC tests concepts through edge cases: inverted pyramids, the edge effect, and which organisms sit at which trophic level. Learn the exceptions as well as the definitions.

days.task: 26 Jan. This is Republic Day: take the day off if you like, but keep the night slot. Finish 'Functions of an Ecosystem': biogeochemical cycles (carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, sulphur) and ecological succession (primary/secondary, hydrarch/xerarch). Cover biomagnification and bioaccumulation in whichever chapter your edition places them. Then SKIM 'Terrestrial Ecosystem' for the features of tundra, forest, grassland and desert only, because Geography has already covered these.
days.pyq: PYQs on the nitrogen cycle, biofertilisers, succession, and the biomagnification of DDT and mercury.
days.tip: Draw the nitrogen cycle once and label the microbe at each step: Rhizobium for fixation, Nitrosomonas for ammonia to nitrite, Nitrobacter for nitrite to nitrate, Pseudomonas for denitrification. UPSC tests which microbe goes with which step.

days.task: 27 Jan. Read the Shankar IAS chapter 'Aquatic Ecosystem': lake zonation, eutrophication, wetlands (their functions, the Ramsar criteria, the Montreux Record), estuaries, mangroves (India's mangrove areas) and coral reefs (types, zooxanthellae, bleaching). Also cover the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 in brief.
days.pyq: PYQs 2013-2025 on wetlands and Ramsar, mangroves, coral reefs and bleaching, and eutrophication.
days.tip: Make a 3-column table of Ramsar site, state and one distinctive feature. Include only sites that appear in PYQs or are very well known, such as Chilika, Keoladeo, Loktak, Wular and Sambhar. Don't memorise the full list. The total number of Indian Ramsar sites keeps changing, so check the latest official count shortly before the exam.

days.task: 28 Jan. Read the Shankar IAS chapter 'Biodiversity': levels of biodiversity, alpha/beta/gamma diversity, megadiverse countries, biodiversity hotspots (India has 4: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Sundaland), threats, in-situ vs ex-situ conservation, and the IUCN Red List categories and criteria.
days.pyq: PYQs on IUCN categories, hotspots, in-situ/ex-situ conservation and threatened species (2013-2025).
days.tip: Write the IUCN categories in order: EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC, DD, NE. Mark that only CR, EN and VU count as 'threatened'. UPSC often hides 'Data Deficient' or 'Near Threatened' in a statement.

days.task: 29 Jan. SKIM 'Indian Biodiversity Diverse Landscape' (the 10 biogeographic zones and their characteristic species) and 'Marine Organism' (plankton, seagrass, seaweed, marine mammals such as the dugong). Read 'Schedule Animals of WPA 1972' only for the logic of the schedules after the 2022 amendment, which reduced them to four. Don't memorise the schedule lists.
days.pyq: PYQs on biogeographic zones, endemic species and marine species (dugong, seagrass).
