days.tip: These chapters are low-yield. Read only the bold lines and the species that already appear in PYQs, and spend no more than 10 minutes on each sub-topic.

days.task: 30 Jan. Heavy 3-hour block: read the Shankar IAS chapter 'Protected Area Network': national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, conservation and community reserves, biosphere reserves (core, buffer and transition zones, and India's UNESCO MAB sites), tiger and elephant reserves, and eco-sensitive zones. Then read 'Conservation Efforts': Project Tiger and the NTCA, Project Elephant, and the crocodile, vulture, Great Indian Bustard and snow leopard programmes. SKIM 'Animal Diversity of India' and 'Plant Diversity of India' only for the species PYQs have asked about. The rest of the day follows the fixed template: 2h PYQs and short notes, 1.5h CSAT, 1h current-affairs consolidation.
days.pyq: 2-hour block: all Environment PYQs 2013-2025 on protected areas, biosphere reserves and tiger reserves, plus the species-in-news and species-location questions. Keep an error log.
days.tip: Keep the Atlas open while you read. Mark every national park and tiger reserve that appears in a PYQ on a blank India map, because UPSC asks location questions such as which PA lies in the Western Ghats or on an international border. Counts of tiger reserves and biosphere reserves keep changing, so update them from official sources before the exam.

days.task: 31 Jan. 9:30-11:30 AM: weekly test (50 questions) on Week 13: Ecology, Functions of an Ecosystem, Terrestrial and Aquatic Ecosystems, Biodiversity, IUCN, Protected Area Network and Conservation Efforts. After the test, analyse your mistakes, revise the Week 13 and Week 12 short notes, and clear any backlog. Evening off.
days.pyq: Re-attempt every PYQ you got wrong this week without looking at the explanations.
days.tip: Sort each mistake into one of three buckets: concept gap, fact not read, or misread statement. Add the deciding fact to your one-page Environment error sheet.

weeks.theme: Environment II: Pollution, Climate Change, Agriculture, Laws, Institutions and Conventions (Shankar IAS Units I, III-V), 1-7 Feb 2027

days.task: 1 Feb. This is Union Budget day: on your commute and at lunch, follow the Budget headlines and keep the summary for Economy revision later, and make a separate note of the environment and green-energy announcements. Night slot: Shankar IAS 'Environmental Pollution', part 1. Cover air pollutants (primary/secondary, PM2.5/PM10, SOx, NOx, ozone, CO), types of smog, indoor pollution, NAAQS and the AQI parameters. Then cover water pollution: BOD, COD, DO, eutrophication, and heavy metals (Minamata and itai-itai diseases).
days.pyq: PYQs on air pollutants, the pollutants used in the AQI, BOD/COD, and heavy-metal diseases (2013-2025).
days.tip: Learn each pollutant as a chain of source, pollutant and health effect: cadmium causes itai-itai, mercury causes Minamata. UPSC frames these as match-the-pair questions.

days.task: 2 Feb. Finish 'Environmental Pollution': soil, noise, thermal, radioactive and e-waste pollution, plus the core principles of the solid, plastic and biomedical waste rules. Then read 'Environmental Issues and Health Effects' for ozone depletion (ODS, ozone hole), acid rain, desertification and fly ash, using whichever chapter your edition places these in. SKIM 'Environmental Impact Assessment' for the stages of the EIA process only. If you run out of time, push the EIA skim to Sunday's backlog slot.
days.pyq: PYQs on ozone depletion, acid rain, e-waste, fly ash and microplastics.
days.tip: Keep 'ozone depletion' and 'global warming' in separate compartments. UPSC likes statements that mix them up: for example, HFCs are greenhouse gases but not significant ozone depleters.

days.task: 3 Feb. Read three Shankar IAS chapters. 'Climate Change': the greenhouse effect, the GHGs and their GWP, sources of methane and N2O, and impacts. 'Ocean Acidification': carbonate chemistry and the effect on corals and shellfish. 'Paris Agreement': NDCs, the goal of holding warming well below 2 degrees C while pursuing 1.5 degrees C, the global stocktake, and the Article 6 markets (concepts only).
days.pyq: PYQs on GHGs, the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement, carbon markets and ocean acidification.
days.tip: Make a one-line timeline of climate diplomacy: UNFCCC 1992, Kyoto 1997, Copenhagen 2009, Paris 2015. UPSC tests which treaty created which mechanism, for example the CDM under Kyoto and NDCs under Paris.

days.task: 4 Feb. Read the Shankar IAS chapter 'Mitigation Strategies': carbon sequestration, CCS, carbon credits and offsets, REDD/REDD+, geoengineering and green buildings. Then read 'India and Climate Change': the eight NAPCC missions, the state action plans, and the structure of India's NDC pledges (not the latest numbers). SKIM 'Climate Change Organisations' and write one line each on what the IPCC, GCF, GEF and Adaptation Fund do.
days.pyq: PYQs on the NAPCC missions, REDD+, the Green Climate Fund and GEF, and carbon sequestration.
days.tip: Memorise the 8 NAPCC missions with a mnemonic. UPSC slips a plausible fake mission into the options.

days.task: 5 Feb. Read the Shankar IAS chapter 'Agriculture': sustainable agriculture, organic and zero-budget natural farming, integrated pest management, biofertilisers (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azolla-Anabaena, mycorrhiza), biopesticides, soil health, and greenhouse gases from agriculture such as methane from paddy. Then SKIM the renewable-energy material in your edition for concepts only: solar, wind, tidal, geothermal, the generations of biofuels, and hydrogen.
days.pyq: PYQs on biofertilisers, organic farming, IPM, crop-residue burning and biofuels.
days.tip: Agriculture-environment questions come from the overlap between Environment and Economy. Link each practice to its environmental benefit, because that is usually the angle the statement takes.

days.task: 6 Feb. Heavy 3-hour block. Read the Shankar IAS chapter 'Acts and Policies': the Wild Life (Protection) Act 1972, Water Act 1974, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, Air Act 1981, Environment (Protection) Act 1986, Biological Diversity Act 2002, Forest Rights Act 2006 and NGT Act 2010. Next read 'Institution and Measures' (CPCB, NBA, NTCA, AWBI, WCCB, NGT) and 'Environmental Organisations' (UNEP, IUCN, WWF, TRAFFIC and others). Finish with 'International Environmental Conventions': Ramsar, CITES, CMS, the CBD with Cartagena and Nagoya, UNCCD, Vienna/Montreal/Kigali, Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm and Minamata. The rest of the day follows the fixed template: 2h PYQs and short notes, 1.5h CSAT, 1h current-affairs consolidation.
days.pyq: 2-hour block: all Environment PYQs 2013-2025 on conventions and protocols, environmental laws and institutions. Build the conventions master table.
days.tip: Build one master table of the conventions with four columns: year, subject, whether it is legally binding, and India's status. UPSC repeatedly asks which of these is legally binding, and it swaps the subjects of Basel, Rotterdam and Stockholm.

days.task: 7 Feb. 9:30-11:30 AM: weekly test (50 questions) on all of Environment, weighted towards Week 14: Pollution, Environmental Issues, Climate Change, the Paris Agreement, Mitigation, NAPCC, Agriculture, Acts, Institutions and Conventions. After the test, analyse your mistakes, revise the Week 14 and Week 13 short notes, and clear any backlog, including the EIA skim if you skipped it on Tuesday. Evening off.
days.pyq: In the afternoon, take a timed set of Environment PYQs from the last 5 years (2021-2025) and compare your accuracy with your Week 13 PYQ error log.
days.tip: Condense the whole subject into 4 pages: the ecology diagrams, the IUCN and protected-area table, the conventions table, and the acts-and-institutions table. In later revision cycles, revise from these pages, not from the book.

howToStudy: Start every chapter with its PYQs. Before reading a Shankar chapter, spend 5 minutes on that topic's 2013-2025 PYQs, then read with the aim of answering what UPSC actually asks. Environment and ecology usually account for about 10-20 questions a year in GS Prelims, more if you count the overlap with Geography and current affairs, and the themes repeat.

Turn anything with many items into a table: conventions (year, subject, binding or not), protected areas (state, feature), acts (year, body created) and pollutants (source, health effect). UPSC builds match-the-pair and 'how many are correct' questions straight from these grids.

Learn the exceptions and qualifiers: which pyramids can be inverted, which IUCN categories count as 'threatened', which gases deplete ozone and which only warm the planet, and which instruments are legally binding. Most wrong answers come from one extreme or swapped word in a statement.

Read with the map: put every national park, tiger reserve, Ramsar site and biosphere reserve that appears in a PYQ on a blank India map, using the Atlas. Location-and-feature questions are common and are easy marks once you have done this.

Skim the low-yield chapters (Terrestrial Ecosystem, Biogeographic Zones, Animal and Plant Diversity, Renewable Energy, EIA) and take only the species and concepts that PYQs have asked about. Don't memorise the full schedule or species lists.

Use Shankar as the static base and treat current affairs as an add-on. When you see a species, COP or report in the news on your commute, file it under the matching Shankar chapter heading in your short notes, not in a separate pile. Counts that keep changing, such as the number of Ramsar sites, tiger reserves and biosphere reserves, must be checked against official sources shortly before the exam, not taken from the book.

Keep the subject's notes to about 4 pages and revise them at least 3 times before Prelims: about 2 months out, 1 month out, and in the last 2 weeks. Use the error sheet from your weekly tests each time.
blocks.scope: Shankar IAS Environment: ecology, biodiversity, protected areas, pollution, climate change, conventions, Indian laws

blocks.name: Science & Tech + Ancient/Medieval

weeks.theme: Science & Technology: NCERT 9-10 basics plus PYQ themes (health, biotech, space, defence, IT, nuclear and energy), 8-14 Feb 2027

days.task: Basic biology, health and diseases (about 75 min). NCERT Class 9 'The Fundamental Unit of Life' (cell organelles: mitochondria, ribosome, lysosome, plastids; prokaryotic vs eukaryotic cells) and 'Why Do We Fall Ill' (pre-2023 edition only; the chapter was dropped in the rationalised edition): infectious vs non-infectious disease; bacterial, viral, protozoan and fungal agents; how vaccines work; why antibiotics do not act on viruses. Add a one-page table: disease, pathogen type, transmission, vaccine (TB, malaria, dengue, HIV, hepatitis B, polio, measles). Optional if time is left: skim 'Tissues'.
days.pyq: S&T PYQs on diseases, vaccines, antibiotics/AMR, probiotics and pathogens (2013-2026). Typical themes: AMR, vaccine types, viral vs bacterial diseases.
days.tip: UPSC asks about mechanisms (why antibiotics fail against viruses, what a vaccine trains), not textbook definitions. Note each disease as pathogen type plus transmission route.

days.task: Biotechnology (about 75 min). NCERT Class 10 'Heredity and Evolution' (pre-2023 edition; called 'Heredity' in the rationalised edition): genes, DNA, traits; skim any evolution part. Skip 'How do Organisms Reproduce?' except the cloning/vegetative propagation idea. Then build biotech notes: DNA/RNA, recombinant DNA, GM crops (Bt cotton, Bt brinjal, GM mustard DMH-11, Golden Rice), CRISPR-Cas9, stem cells (embryonic vs adult/iPSC), gene therapy, cloning (SCNT, Dolly), mRNA vaccines, mitochondrial replacement therapy, DNA fingerprinting.
days.pyq: Biotech PYQs (2013-2026): Bt crops, GM mustard, stem cells, CRISPR, 'three-parent baby', genome sequencing, biofortification, cloning.
days.tip: For every technology write three lines: what it is, one Indian application, one controversy or regulator (GEAC). Statement questions catch you on over-claims like 'can cure all genetic diseases'.

days.task: Space technology (about 75 min). Note: NCERT Class 9 'Gravitation' does not cover escape velocity or orbits; skim it only for the universal law of gravitation, free fall and mass vs weight , and take orbits from your notes source. Then notes on orbit types (LEO, MEO, GEO vs GSO, polar sun-synchronous, GTO), Lagrange points L1-L5, launch vehicles (PSLV, GSLV, LVM3, SSLV; cryogenic stage), Indian missions (Chandrayaan-1/2/3, Mangalyaan, Aditya-L1, AstroSat, XPoSat), NavIC/IRNSS vs GAGAN, space debris, reusable launch vehicles, and a short note on black holes and gravitational waves (LIGO-India).
days.pyq: Space PYQs (2013-2026): IRNSS/NavIC, Mars Orbiter Mission, Lagrange points, GSAT/cryogenic engine, black holes and gravitational waves, space debris.
days.tip: Draw one orbit diagram with altitudes and uses. UPSC often swaps uses between orbits (remote sensing vs communication), so learn which orbit suits which job.

days.task: Defence technology (about 75 min). Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (Agni, Prithvi, Akash, Nag, Trishul), ballistic vs cruise missiles, BrahMos (India-Russia), hypersonic glide vehicles, ballistic missile defence, MIRV basics, stealth, drones/UAVs, India's nuclear triad (concept only). Add a 15-min skim of NCERT Class 10 'Magnetic Effects of Electric Current' (electromagnet; motor and generator principle, which are only in the pre-2023 edition) and the Class 9 'Sound' sections on ultrasound and SONAR (use the pre-2023 edition if your copy lacks them).
days.pyq: Defence and physics-application PYQs (2013-2026): missile types, SONAR/ultrasound, drones, plus physics basics behind them.
days.tip: Make a missile table: name, type (ballistic/cruise/SAM/anti-tank), range class, developer. Statement questions test the type and the joint developer, not exact ranges.

days.task: Nuclear and energy (about 75 min). NCERT Class 10 'Sources of Energy' (pre-2023 edition only: conventional vs non-conventional, solar cells, nuclear fission vs fusion) and 'Electricity' (skim: only power, resistance in series/parallel basics). Then India's three-stage nuclear programme (PHWR on natural uranium, fast breeder reactors on plutonium, thorium/U-233), heavy water, enrichment, fuel cells, green hydrogen, batteries (Li-ion vs sodium-ion), perovskite solar cells.
days.pyq: Nuclear and energy PYQs (2013-2026): three-stage programme, thorium, fuel cells, hydrogen, solar PV materials, battery chemistries, IAEA safeguards.
days.tip: Learn the logic of the three stages (each stage produces the fuel for the next). Then fertile vs fissile and PHWR vs FBR follow without memorising.

days.task: Heavy block (3h). (1) IT and emerging tech, about 1.5h: AI/ML and generative AI, blockchain and cryptocurrency, quantum computing and cryptography, 5G, IoT, cloud and edge computing, semiconductors and chip fabrication, LiFi/Wi-Fi, Bluetooth/NFC, 3D printing. (2) NCERT Class 10 'Carbon and its Compounds' (allotropes: diamond, graphite, fullerene; link to graphene and nanotechnology), about 30 min. (3) NCERT Class 10 'Light - Reflection and Refraction' (skim for concepts, skip numericals) and 'The Human Eye and the Colourful World' (scattering, dispersion, rainbow, defects of vision), about 1h. The term-only skim of 'Motion', 'Force and Laws of Motion', 'Work and Energy', 'Chemical Reactions and Equations', 'Acids, Bases and Salts' and 'Metals and Non-metals' is optional backlog, done only through PYQs that touch them. Then 2h PYQs and short notes, 1.5h CSAT, 1h weekly current-affairs consolidation (S&T news themes).
days.pyq: Thematic S&T PYQ sweep (2011-2026): IT/emerging tech, nanotech/graphene, optics phenomena, everyday chemistry, about 40-50 questions with full review. Then make one-page short notes on everything you got wrong.
days.tip: For new technologies UPSC asks what the tech can and cannot do. Note one limitation for each (e.g., blockchain is not necessarily public, quantum computers do not replace classical ones).

days.task: 9:30-11:30 AM weekly test on all of Week 15 S&T (diseases, biotech, space, defence, nuclear/energy, IT, NCERT basics). Then mistake analysis, sorting each error as concept gap, careless or guess. Revise the Week 15 short notes and the Week 14 notes. Clear backlog, especially any NCERT chapter you only skimmed. Evening off.
days.pyq: Re-attempt every S&T PYQ marked wrong during the week, without looking at notes.
days.tip: Keep an 'S&T traps' list of extreme words (only, all, never) and swapped uses. Read it again before every future S&T test.

weeks.theme: Ancient & Medieval India, PYQ-driven (old NCERT R.S. Sharma and Satish Chandra, high-frequency topics only), 15-21 Feb 2027

days.task: Indus Valley and the Vedic age (about 75 min). R.S. Sharma (old NCERT 'Ancient India'): the Harappan Culture chapter (town planning, Great Bath, sites and their state/river, seals, trade, script, decline) and the Rig Vedic and Later Vedic chapters (tribal polity, Sabha/Samiti/Vidatha, varna, rivers, the four Vedas, Brahmanas, Upanishads). Skip the historiography and sources chapters. Stone Age and Chalcolithic chapters (Bhimbetka, Mehrgarh, Inamgaon only) move to Sunday backlog, via PYQs only.
days.pyq: IVC and Vedic PYQs (2013-2026): site features, Harappan crafts and trade, Vedic terms and texts, Upanishadic ideas.
days.tip: Make a site-to-feature-to-state table (Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi). UPSC pairs sites with features, and terms like Sabha/Samiti with their roles.

days.task: Buddhism, Jainism and other heterodox sects (about 75 min). R.S. Sharma: 'Jainism and Buddhism' chapter. Cover: Mahavira and the tirthankaras, Shvetambara vs Digambara, triratna, anekantavada and syadvada; the Buddha's life, Four Noble Truths, Eightfold Path, the four Buddhist councils (place, king, president), Hinayana/Mahayana/Vajrayana, Bodhisattvas, Pali and Prakrit canons; Ajivikas and Charvaka/Lokayata. Skim the chapter on territorial states and the rise of Magadha (16 Mahajanapadas and capitals only).
days.pyq: Buddhism and Jainism PYQs (2013-2026), one of the most frequently asked ancient areas: councils, Bodhisattvas, philosophical terms, sects, Buddhist sites.
days.tip: UPSC asks concept terms (anekantavada, nirvana, paramitas) and which sect believes what. Write a three-column compare table (Jain, Buddhist, Vedic) for common concepts.

days.task: Mauryas and post-Mauryan India (about 75 min). R.S. Sharma: the Maurya chapters (Chandragupta, Kautilya's Arthashastra, Megasthenes' Indica, Ashoka's dhamma, Major and Minor Rock Edicts, pillar edicts, languages and scripts, administration). Then 'Central Asian Contacts and their Results' (Kushanas, Kanishka, Gandhara and Mathura schools) and 'The Age of the Satavahanas' (land grants, Nashik/Nanaghat inscriptions). Skip 'Iranian and Macedonian Invasions' unless a PYQ points to it.
days.pyq: Maurya and post-Maurya PYQs (2013-2026): Ashokan inscriptions, dhamma, Arthashastra terms, Kushana art schools, Satavahana features.
days.tip: Ashokan edicts are asked by content and location (e.g., which edict names Ashoka). Keep a small table: edict, location, key content.

days.task: Guptas and Sangam age (about 75 min). R.S. Sharma: 'Rise and Growth of the Gupta Empire' and 'Life in the Gupta Age' (administration, agraharas and land grants, Kalidasa, Aryabhata, Varahamihira, coinage, Nalanda). 'Harsha and his Times' (skim: Hiuen Tsang only). Sangam: 'The Dawn of History in the Deep South' (Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas; Sangam literature, Tolkappiyam, tinai landscapes, Indo-Roman trade at Arikamedu/Muziris).
days.pyq: Gupta and Sangam PYQs (2013-2026): Gupta-era science and literature, land grants, Sangam terms, foreign travellers.
days.tip: For Sangam, UPSC asks terms and texts, not dynastic lists. Learn about 10 Sangam words with meanings and the three kingdoms' emblems and ports.

days.task: South Indian kingdoms and temple architecture (about 75 min). Satish Chandra (old NCERT 'Medieval India'): 'Northern India: Age of the Three Empires' (tripartite struggle among Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas, skim) and 'South India: The Chola Empire' (Chola local self-government: ur, sabha, nadu, Uttaramerur inscriptions; naval expeditions; Brihadeshvara). Add Pallavas (Mamallapuram rathas, Kanchi) and Badami Chalukyas (Aihole, Pattadakal) from R.S. Sharma's chapter on new states in the peninsula. Add temple styles: Nagara, Dravida, Vesara (from your Art & Culture notes).
days.pyq: South Indian dynasties and temple-architecture PYQs (2013-2026): Chola administration, Pallava and Chalukya monuments, temple styles. Overlaps with Art & Culture PYQs.
days.tip: Link each dynasty to one monument and one administrative feature. UPSC mixes Art & Culture with history here, so revise the temple-style chart.

days.task: Heavy block (3h). Satish Chandra: read 'Government, and Economic and Social Life under the Delhi Sultanat' fully; from 'The Delhi Sultanat I and II' read only the reform sections (Iltutmish and the iqta, Balban, Alauddin Khalji's market reforms, Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token currency and capital shift, Firoz Shah's canals). 'The Age of Vijayanagara and the Bahmanids, and the Coming of the Portuguese' (nayankara, amaram, Krishnadevaraya, Hampi). From 'Struggle for Empire in North India II', only Sher Shah's administration. 'The Age of Akbar' (mansabdari, zabt/dahsala, Din-i-Ilahi, Ibadat Khana). For the Marathas, read only the Shivaji administration section (Ashtapradhan, chauth/sardeshmukhi) inside the 'Climax and Disintegration of the Mughal Empire' chapters, and skip the rest of those chapters, 'India and the World' and 'Struggle for Empire in North India I'. 'Economic and Social Life under the Mughals' goes to backlog, via PYQs only. In the 2h PYQ block, read the Bhakti-Sufi sections of 'Cultural Development in India' (Sultanate period) and 'Cultural and Religious Developments' (Mughal period) through PYQs. Then 1.5h CSAT and 1h weekly current-affairs consolidation.
days.pyq: Medieval PYQs (2013-2026): Sultanate administration and revenue terms, Vijayanagara, Mughal institutions, Bhakti saints and Sufi silsilas, foreign travellers (Ibn Battuta, Nicolo Conti, Bernier). Make short notes on the misses.
days.tip: Medieval questions are terms-heavy: iqta, khalisa, mansab, zabt, amaram. Keep a glossary of term, meaning and who introduced or used it. That list covers most of the answers.

days.task: 9:30-11:30 AM weekly test on Week 16 Ancient and Medieval (IVC to Mughals plus Bhakti-Sufi). Mistake analysis. Revise the Week 16 tables (sites, councils, edicts, terms glossary) and the Week 15 S&T short notes. Clear backlog: Stone Age/Chalcolithic via PYQs, and if time, a 20-min skim of the six orthodox schools of philosophy (Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, Vedanta) from R.S. Sharma's philosophy chapter. Evening off.
days.pyq: Re-attempt all wrong Ancient/Medieval PYQs from the week, then 15 mixed S&T PYQs from Week 15 for spaced revision.
days.tip: Ancient and medieval give fewer marks per hour than Polity or Economy. If short of time, prioritise Buddhism/Jainism, temple architecture and the medieval glossary, the areas UPSC asks most often.

howToStudy: Start each S&T theme with its PYQs, then the NCERT basics. UPSC tests concepts and applications (what a technology does, why something happens), not formulas or numerical data.
Make one-page comparison tables, not paragraph notes: orbit vs use, missile vs type, disease vs pathogen, site vs feature, edict vs content, dynasty vs monument.
In S&T statement questions, watch for extreme words ('only', 'all', 'cannot') and swapped applications. Most wrong options over-claim what a technology can do.

Ancient/Medieval is PYQ-driven. Read only the topics that appear repeatedly in 2013-2026 papers (Buddhism/Jainism, Ashoka, Sangam, Chola administration, Sultanate/Mughal terms, Bhakti-Sufi) and skim dynastic chronology.
Keep a running glossary of historical terms (sabha, ur, iqta, mansab, zabt, amaram, tinai). In Prelims GS Paper I, history questions test terms, concepts and pairings far more often than dates.
Link history with Art & Culture as you study: tie each dynasty to its monuments, art school or literature, because UPSC frames many questions across both.

Use commute time for S&T current affairs, but file each news item under a static theme (space, biotech, defence, health, IT, energy) so it revises the basics instead of becoming separate notes. Several NCERT science chapters and sections used here ('Why Do We Fall Ill', 'Sources of Energy', motor/generator) exist only in the pre-2023 editions, so keep those older PDFs.

blocks.name: CSAT

weeks.theme: Diagnostic + Number System I

days.task: First 30 min: attempt a 25-question mixed diagnostic from CSAT 2024 under time pressure, then note which topics are weak. Next 60 min: Number System I, covering divisibility rules (2-11), unit digit cyclicity (2,3,7,8 repeat every 4; 4,9 every 2; 0,1,5,6 never change) and basic remainders.
days.pyq: CSAT 2024 (first 25 Qs as diagnostic) + Number System Qs from CSAT 2019-2021
days.tip: For a unit digit, use only the last digit of the base and take the power mod 4. If the remainder is 0, use the 4th term of the cycle. Start a formula sheet tonight and add to it every week.

weeks.theme: Number System II

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages . Then HCF/LCM word problems (bells tolling, tiles, largest measuring length), factors and counting factors, digit-based problems, trailing zeroes in n!, and remainder theorems.
days.pyq: Number System Qs from CSAT 2015-2018 and 2022-2023
days.tip: Trailing zeroes in n! = [n/5] + [n/25] + [n/125]... UPSC digit puzzles often fall faster if you test the options than if you set up algebra.

weeks.theme: Percentages, Profit-Loss, Discount

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then fraction-percentage equivalents (1/6=16.67%, 1/7=14.29%, 1/8=12.5%), successive change, price-consumption, marked price, discount, profit/loss, and dishonest dealer problems.
days.pyq: Percentage and Profit-Loss Qs from CSAT 2016-2023
days.tip: Use multiplying factors: +20% = x1.2 and -15% = x0.85. For successive changes a and b, net = a + b + ab/100 (use negative signs for decreases). Most of these questions take one line with factors.

weeks.theme: Ratio, Proportion, Mixtures, Averages

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then ratio and proportion, partnership, ages, alligation and mixtures, averages (including adding or removing a member), and weighted averages.
days.pyq: Ratio, Ages and Average Qs from CSAT 2014-2023
days.tip: Alligation solves any weighted-average problem: cross-subtract from the mean to get the ratio. With averages, track the change in the total, not the averages themselves.

weeks.theme: Simple & Compound Interest + RC Technique I

days.task: 45 min SI/CI: the CI-SI difference for 2 and 3 years, doubling time, and installments. 45 min RC technique: read the question stem first, identify the main idea, and practise 4 passages.
days.pyq: Interest Qs from CSAT 2013-2022 + 4 RC passages from CSAT 2022
days.tip: CI - SI for 2 years = P(r/100)^2; for 3 years = P(r/100)^2 x (3 + r/100). In RC, the right answer is supported by the passage itself. Options that sound correct only from outside knowledge are traps.

weeks.theme: Time, Speed, Distance

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then relative speed, trains crossing poles, platforms and each other, boats and streams, average speed over equal distances, and circular tracks.
days.pyq: TSD Qs from CSAT 2014-2023
days.tip: km/h x 5/18 = m/s. Add speeds when moving in opposite directions and subtract when moving the same way. Average speed over two equal distances = 2xy/(x+y), never (x+y)/2.

weeks.theme: Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then time and work using the LCM total-work method, people joining or leaving midway, wages in proportion to work done, and pipes and cisterns where leaks count as negative work.
days.pyq: Time & Work Qs from CSAT 2013-2023
days.tip: Take total work = LCM of the day counts, so each person's daily output is a whole number. This removes fractions and roughly halves your solving time.

weeks.theme: RC II + Critical Reasoning

days.task: 60 min RC, focused on inference, assumption, central theme, author's view and the most logical corollary (6 passages). 30 min statement-assumption and statement-course-of-action questions.
days.pyq: 6 RC passages from CSAT 2023; use the remaining 2023 and 2024 passages as the 2-passage warm-ups in later weeks
days.tip: Reject options that are extreme (always, never, only), go beyond the passage's scope, or are true but not what was asked. An assumption is the unstated premise the argument cannot stand without.

weeks.theme: Permutation, Combination & Probability

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then the fundamental counting principle, arrangements with repeated letters, selections (nCr), handshakes and diagonals, and basic probability with dice, coins and cards.
days.pyq: P&C and Probability Qs from CSAT 2015-2024
days.tip: Ask yourself first whether order matters: if yes it is a permutation, if no it is a combination. For small cases, listing outcomes by hand beats formulas and avoids double counting.

weeks.theme: Syllogisms, Statement-Conclusion, Venn Diagrams

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then syllogisms (all/some/no, possibility cases), statement-conclusion questions, and Venn diagram counting with 2-3 sets.
days.pyq: Syllogism and Logical Reasoning Qs from CSAT 2016-2024
days.tip: Draw the minimum-overlap Venn diagram. A conclusion follows only if it holds in every valid diagram. 'Some A are not B' follows from 'Some A are C' plus 'No C is B'.

weeks.theme: Blood Relations, Direction Sense, Coding-Decoding

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then blood relations (family-tree notation), coded relations (A+B, A*B), direction and distance with right and left turns, shadow-based direction questions, and letter and number coding.
days.pyq: Blood Relation, Direction and Coding Qs from CSAT 2012-2023
days.tip: Always draw it: square for male, circle for female, horizontal line for siblings, vertical line for generations. For directions, mark coordinates on a grid and use Pythagoras for the final distance.

weeks.theme: Seating Arrangement, Puzzles, Ranking

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then linear and circular seating (facing the centre or facing outward), floor and box puzzles, ranking and ordering, and grid-based scheduling puzzles.
days.pyq: Arrangement and Puzzle Qs from CSAT 2018-2024
days.tip: Place the definite clues first, then branch into at most 2 cases. In circular seating facing the centre, the person's left is clockwise (facing outward, it is anticlockwise). Abandon a puzzle set that has not resolved within 4 minutes.

weeks.theme: Clocks, Calendars, Series & Patterns

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then clock angles, how often the hands coincide or are opposite, odd days and day-of-week calculations, leap years, and number, letter and figure series.
days.pyq: Clock, Calendar and Series Qs from CSAT 2013-2023
days.tip: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. The hands coincide 22 times a day and are opposite 22 times a day. A non-leap year has 1 odd day and a leap year has 2. Odd days in 100/200/300/400 years = 5/3/1/0.

weeks.theme: Data Interpretation + Data Sufficiency

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then tables, bar and pie charts, line graphs, percentage-change comparisons, approximation, and data sufficiency (whether statement I alone, II alone, or both together are enough).
days.pyq: DI and Data Sufficiency Qs from CSAT 2015-2024
days.tip: Approximate aggressively and compare ratios without fully computing them. In data sufficiency, never solve to the final number: you only need to know whether a unique answer exists.

weeks.theme: Timed Mock I (half paper) + Analysis

days.task: Timed half-paper: CSAT 2025 Q1-40 (any one booklet series) in 60 min, in exam-hall conditions with OMR-style marking. 30 min analysis: classify each error as concept, calculation, misread or time-sink, and update the formula sheet.
days.pyq: CSAT 2025, Questions 1-40
days.tip: Use a 3-round strategy: round 1 for RC and easy quant, round 2 for medium questions, round 3 for leftovers. Target the 66.67 cut-off plus a 20-25 mark buffer, not 200. Each wrong answer costs 1/3 of the question's marks, so don't blind-guess.

weeks.theme: Timed Mock II (half paper) + Consolidation

days.task: Timed half-paper: CSAT 2025 Q41-80 in 60 min. 30 min: finalise a one-page formula and trap sheet and list your two weakest quant topics for Week 17 onwards.
days.pyq: CSAT 2025, Questions 41-80
days.tip: Add both halves for an estimated score. If you are below 80, spend the next 4 Saturdays' CSAT slots on RC plus your two weakest quant topics rather than new topics. Prioritise RC questions, which give the highest accuracy per minute.

weeks.theme: Geometry, Mensuration, Cubes & Dice, Linear Equations

days.task: Warm-up: 2 RC passages. Then basic mensuration (area and perimeter of rectangle, triangle, circle; volume and surface area of cube, cuboid, cylinder), painted-cube cutting, dice (opposite faces), and simple linear-equation word problems. Then fix the maintenance schedule: from Week 18, on alternate Saturdays (Weeks 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28), take one full 2-hour CSAT paper by extending the 1.5 h CSAT slot with 30 min from the PYQ + notes block.
days.pyq: Mensuration, Cube/Dice and Equation Qs from CSAT 2013-2024
days.tip: A painted cube cut into n x n x n small cubes has 8 cubes with 3 painted faces, 12(n-2) with 2, 6(n-2)^2 with 1, and (n-2)^3 with none. For equation problems, plug the options in before writing any algebra. For the full papers, use CSAT 2022, 2021, 2020 and 2019 plus 2 fresh test-series mocks, because the 2023-2025 papers are already partly used.

howToStudy: CSAT is qualifying (33% = 66.67/200), but it eliminates many candidates who are ready for GS. Treat it as non-negotiable: aim for a safe 90+ and stop chasing 150.

Reading comprehension is roughly 30-40% of recent papers (about 25-30 of 80 questions) and the most reliable source of marks. Do 2 passages every session and answer strictly from the passage. Reject extreme, out-of-scope, or 'true but irrelevant' options.

Learn each quant topic through UPSC PYQs (2011-2025), not through bank-exam books. UPSC questions are puzzle-like and rely on logic, so after each attempt ask whether option-testing would have been faster.

Keep a single one-page formula and trap sheet: cyclicity, the fraction-percentage table, CI-SI difference, relative speed, clock angle, odd days, nCr, painted-cube counts. Revise it every Sunday and add every new mistake to it.

Practise against the clock. You get 120 min for 80 questions, which is 1.5 min per question, so abandon any single question that is unresolved after about 3 min. Each wrong answer costs 1/3 of the question's marks (0.83 of 2.5). A blind guess among 4 options gains nothing on average, so guess only after eliminating at least one option, and ideally two.

Keep an error log tagged by cause (concept, calculation, misread, time-sink). Many CSAT marks are lost to misreading ('NOT', 'at least', 'how many are correct'), so underline the key words in every question stem.

From Week 18 to Prelims, take one full timed CSAT paper every alternate Saturday (Weeks 18-28, 6 papers). Aim to score 90+ in at least 4 of them. If you don't, move one weekly GS PYQ session to CSAT practice until you do.
